gaps.structure: Direct nucleus-to-cell-surface mechanical edge: the unilateral steric bearing (non-penetration) contact of the cortex / plasma membrane on the nuclear envelope, plus the perinuclear cytolinker strut anchoring the nucleus to the cortex. This is the load path by which cortical contraction and cell flattening COMPRESS the nucleus, and by which the nucleus resists being cut through by a crumpling cortex.
gaps.connects: `nucleus` <-> `cortex` (and `nucleus` <-> `membrane`). Both component pairs are ABSENT from the graph: measured neighbours of `nucleus` are exactly {cytosol, intermediate_filament, microtubule, sf_arc} (contracts.py:268-272, 291, 298, 311). Live enumeration of absent nucleus pairs: ('cortex','nucleus'), ('membrane','nucleus'), plus focal_adhesion/lamellipodium/filopodium/nmii/ecm/world_boundary.
gaps.why_architecture_cannot_express_it: The architecture's own rules make an undeclared component pair inexpressible: 'All inter-component mechanics goes through connector or field-coupling objects' (CELL_ENGINE_ARCHITECTURE.md:90-91) and the acceptance gate 'no component can mutate another component's state except through a registered connector/coupler' (CELL_ENGINE_ARCHITECTURE.md:211), on top of the PI rule that co-location in a shared array is NEVER a connection. There is therefore no legal way for the cortex to bear on the nuclear envelope. The three existing routes do not substitute: (1) LINC (connectors 8/9/11) is by the project's own definition 'a *distinct* force family (an attractive/elastic tether along the LINC bond), NOT a steric term' (ac/solid/INTEGRATION.md:92-93) - a bilateral discrete bond population cannot impose a one-sided non-penetration constraint, and it reaches the cortex only in series through sf_arc/MT; (2) the cytosol Biot/Darcy field (connectors 3+4) transmits normal load only transiently - with intracellular poroelastic diffusivity D_p ~ 40-60 um^2/s (Moeendarbary 2013, cited at docs/v2_audit/KB_UPLOAD_MANIFEST_2026-07-15.md:239), tau ~ L^2/D_p ~ 0.1-0.6 s for L = 2-5 um, so on the seconds-to-minutes timescale of spreading and crawling the pore pressure drains and provides no steady-state resistance to interpenetration; (3) the CONTACT family exists but is instanced on only 3 pairs (lamellipodium-membrane, filopodium-membrane, membrane-ecm), none nuclear. The nucleus geometry provider even retains its 642-node mesh explicitly 'for geometry, collision, pressure quadrature, strain visualization' (cell_engine/FLUID_CORE_PLAN.md:21-22) - collision geometry provisioned with NO consumer connector. And the structure that historically carried this load was deliberately re-routed away from the cortex: 'The cortex anchor is not the registered composition. The common engine graph declares `if_nucleus_linc` and `if_sf_plectin`; the legacy wrapper hard-wires a nearest-cortex spring instead of an SF/arc plectin endpoint' (cell_engine/INTERMEDIATE_FILAMENT_PLAN.md:53-55), whereas the legacy module described that same spoke as 'the nucleus<->cortex load path that fixes the mechanically-DECOUPLED nucleus' (ac/solid/intermediate_filament.py:3-7). This is an architecture-layer decision, not a ladder rung.
gaps.observable_that_would_be_wrong: Nuclear compression by the cell surface. The project has already MEASURED the failure natively: under physiological plate compression the cortex deformed (max 751 nm) while 'nucleus flattening under the plate: **0.0 %** (z-half 5.106 -> 5.106 um) - the nucleus does not deform', verdict 'the interior (nucleus + MT aster) is mechanically DECOUPLED from the cortex' (docs/v2_audit/INTERNAL_DISPLACEMENT_DIAGNOSIS_2026-07-16.md:13-22). Second observable, exactly PI example (i): a cortex asked to 'crumple as one object' has no stop against the nuclear envelope, so the dorsal cortex/membrane passes through the nucleus during retraction or bleb collapse - there is no non-penetration constraint anywhere in the graph for that pair. Third: nuclear height/aspect vs spread area (the oblate MCF7 flatten gate, ac/nucleus/INTEGRATION.md:84-88) can only be produced by pulling on discrete LINC anchors, never by the surface bearing on the envelope, so the recorded 'K_nuc ~ 25 nN/um -> 5-6 nN cap ~ 0.2 um ~ 10x short' shortfall is the signature of a missing bearing path rather than a magnitude problem.

confirmed_sufficient: CRAWL FORCE DIPOLE CLOSES - not a gap. Front: lamellipodium -> (17) lamellipodium_membrane_contact (Brownian-ratchet on the membrane) and -> (20) lamellipodium_nascent_fa -> focal_adhesion -> (6) integrin_collagen_clutch -> ecm -> (31) ecm_far_field_anchor -> world_boundary. Rear: nmii -> (25) nmii_sf_motor -> sf_arc -> (5) fa_actin_anchor -> focal_adhesion -> (6) -> ecm. Cell body carried by (7) sf_cortex_transient, (1) membrane_erm_cortex, (18) lamellipodium_cortex_seam, (2/3/4) fluid boundaries, (8/9/11) LINC. world_boundary is reachable from all 13 components (verified with force_path()). Net translation needs asymmetric front/rear adhesion lifetime, which is kinetic inside connector 6 (kinetics=True, commit_on_accept=True, generation_required/remap_on_accept/blocks_sleep_refine - contracts.py:279-283): a rate law, not a structure.

ECM REMODELLING BY A PROTRUDING LAMELLIPODIUM - not a gap; PI example (ii) is expressible. Fiber realignment/densification emerges from (6) clutch pull + (30) ecm_crosslink (kinetic, generation_required, remap_on_accept) + (32) membrane_ecm_contact steric push; the collagen owner already declares 'crosslink kinetics, fiber remodelling, damage, refinement/coarsening' and per-segment damage history as COMPONENT-INTERNAL state (cell_engine/ECM_WORLD_PLAN.md:27, :48, :211-226). Proteolysis (MMP) is a kinetic degradation process acting on that internal damage variable - class (iv), not a load-bearing structure. Note the correct routing: lamellipodial actin does NOT need an edge to ecm because the plasma membrane is physically interposed; lam -> (17) membrane -> (32) ecm is the faithful path.

SUBSTRATE / DISH / 2D COMPLIANT GEL - not a missing component; this is `ecm` instanced differently (class ii). The baseline is a live collagen world with a `far_field_dirichlet` boundary (ECM_WORLD_PLAN.md:81-83) and a fixed substrate anchor is explicitly production-FORBIDDEN ('ff/fa_clutch_warp.py fixed substrate anchor | production 폐기', ECM_WORLD_PLAN.md:300). Substrate stiffness is a property of the ECM fiber/crosslink card, not a new state owner. `world_boundary` (owns_geometry=False, dynamically_evolving=False, contracts.py:246-250) correctly supplies the single far-field reference and correctly has degree 1: for an adherent cell EVERY external reaction must pass through the matrix.

EXTRACELLULAR MEDIUM / CULTURE FLUID - mechanically negligible (class iii). Regime is Re ~ 1e-13 (docs/v2_audit/DYNAMIC_FEM_CFD_UPGRADE_ROADMAP_2026-07-15.md:58; inertialess architecture, LITERATURE_POSITIONING_2026-07-20.md:37-40), so outer-medium viscous drag is orders below clutch traction; outside pressure and osmolarity are Dirichlet data on connector (3) membrane_cytosol_boundary, and PI already ratified the osmotic term as a CONSTANT delta-pi = 40 Pa with sigma=1 and no volume coupling (2026-07-23). A scalar boundary condition is not a state-owning component.

CELL-CELL JUNCTIONS: cadherin adherens junctions, desmosomes, tight junctions, gap junctions - out of scope (class v). There is no second cell in the composition; such a connector needs an endpoint on another cell's membrane/cortex/IF. This is the single-cell platform; multicellular junctions belong to the DCM engine (cadherin cluster/maturation work lives in dcm/, and PI 2026-06-21 fixed cadherin there as a KU-4.2 catch-bond).

CONTRACTILE RING / MITOTIC SPINDLE / CELL-CYCLE MACHINERY - out of scope for the stated target and, where in scope, component-internal. PI named INTERPHASE as the state to fit. A cytokinetic ring is an equatorial NMII+actin PATTERN inside the existing `cortex` + `nmii` owners on the same (26) nmii_cortex_motor edge; the spindle is `microtubule` internal topology with the existing (9)/(10) edges. Neither needs a new component or a new component pair.

CHROMATIN, LAMIN-A/C, LAMIN-B, NUCLEOLUS - nucleus-internal (given, and confirmed: contracts.py:212 'native lamina/chromatin FEM'; forces_manifest.py:244 nucleus_chromatin_modulus; CELL_ENGINE_ARCHITECTURE.md:63 'chromatin relaxation and damage state' listed as local/internal). Envelope rupture and lamin softening are constitutive/damage state on that owner, not new load paths.

MICROVILLI / MEMBRANE FOLDS / RUFFLES / BLEB - membrane-internal Raucher-Sheetz area reservoir (given; CELL_ENGINE_ARCHITECTURE.md:60 'area reservoir, curvature state'). A bleb is an emergent ERM-detachment event on the EXISTING (1) membrane_erm_cortex edge plus (3) fluid boundary; the project already validated bleb nucleation on exactly that pairing (a_crit = 2*gamma/delta-P), which is positive evidence the pair suffices.

CROSSLINKERS (alpha-actinin, filamin, fascin, plectin, spectraplakin, spectrin/ankyrin membrane skeleton) - connectors 12/13/29/30 plus component-internal crosslink KMC (given). Cortex is declared 'explicit crosslinked F-actin network' (contracts.py:204); lamellipodium/filopodium declare 'excluded volume, branch-angle energy, explicit cross-link mechanics' as the ACTOR's private terms (cell_engine/PROTRUSION_PLAN.md:47, :62). Intra-component crosslinks are correctly not edges: both endpoints have one owner.

POLYMERISATION KINETICS: nucleation, Arp2/3 branching, capping, severing, formin elongation, treadmilling, turnover, dynamic instability - all class (iv) kinetic processes on component-internal state, and the architecture explicitly defers WHICH component owns which event kernel to a per-component biology phase with a sourced rate (contracts.py:191-196: 'Every component is declared has_events=False ... the flag is flipped then, not here'). None is a load-bearing structure.

MTOC / CENTROSOME - microtubule-internal retained rigid block, not a component ('MTOC minus-end anchoring and reaction'; 'The MTOC is a retained rigid translation/orientation block', cell_engine/MICROTUBULE_PLAN.md:184-189), with its envelope attachment already carried by (9) mt_nucleus_linc.

ORGANELLE PASSENGERS (mitochondria, ER, Golgi, endosomes, lipid droplets) - class (iii). Advected cargo whose mechanical role for a single adherent cell is to modify cytosol permeability/storage, which is `cytosol` constitutive state (CELL_ENGINE_ARCHITECTURE.md:62 'constitutive permeability/storage'). Each as a component would add ~3 mandatory edges for no measurable traction or stiffness change.

IF-TO-SUBSTRATE PATH (the runner-up; still arguable away). Keratin/vimentin DOES reach the matrix: (12) if_sf_plectin -> sf_arc -> (5) fa_actin_anchor -> focal_adhesion -> (6) integrin_collagen_clutch -> ecm, a genuine 3-connector tensile series, every hop kinetic, bidirectional and adjoint. The direct hemidesmosomal route (alpha6beta4 + plectin + keratin) is a PARALLEL path, so its absence changes stiffness partitioning, not connectedness - and its ligand is laminin-332, not in the declared ECM ligand card ('alpha2beta1_collagen', contracts.py:281), making it a ligand/parameter-card scope question on the collagen-I baseline. Vimentin-plectin-1f at focal adhesions (Burgstaller et al. 2010, MBoC 21:3362) would likewise be one extra PLECTIN-family edge with a different endpoint pair, not a new component. Recorded as the second-strongest candidate.

CORTEX-TO-ADHESION and MEMBRANE-TO-ADHESION - not gaps. cortex reaches focal_adhesion by two independent series routes ((7) sf_cortex_transient -> (5); and (18) lamellipodium_cortex_seam -> (20)); the membrane reaches it via (1) ERM -> cortex -> (7) -> (5). The bilayer's own load transfer through the integrin transmembrane domain is second-order to the talin-actin link: AFFECTS_MAGNITUDE at worst. Same reasoning retires MT-vs-membrane: the MT-cortex pair already EXISTS ((10) mt_cortex_capture), so a steric plus-end end-stop is a second force law on an already-permitted pair - an in-architecture extension, exactly as SURFACE_BODY_PLAN.md:219 adds a contact coupler to the already-declared membrane-cortex pair. That is the principled line applied throughout, and it is why only the nucleus (a pair that exists NOWHERE) survived it.

CONNECTOR ECONOMY - the decisive structural argument for sufficiency. Under 'co-location is never a connection', a new component is mechanically inert until it carries >= 2 load edges plus a cytosol immersed-transfer edge: ~3 new bidirectional+adjoint+snapshot/rollback/commit obligations each. The graph averages 32/13 = 2.46 edges per component; the four components a critic might add (medium, substrate, organelle, junction partner) would push 32 -> ~44 edges. Meanwhile today's audit measures the DECLARED graph as '9 force-real, 4 one-sided, 19 declared-only', 'only 5 runtime objects ever constructed outside tests/', and 'Net: 2 of 32 connectors dispatched' in the only composed build (docs/v2_audit/AUDIT_AC_ENGINE_2026-07-25.md:44, :64). A smaller component set with closed connectors strictly dominates a larger set with declared-only edges - which is exactly the PI's stated priority.

IMPLEMENTATION-STATUS ITEMS THAT ARE NOT ARCHITECTURE GAPS, each a rung on the 8-state ladder tracked separately: LINC family 'KERNEL_BOUND in a vacuum, zero runtime callers' (AUDIT_AC_ENGINE_2026-07-25.md:52); ecm_crosslink 'No crosslink force kernel exists anywhere in the tree' (:56); the 8 protrusion edges CONTRACTED with owners never constructed (:50, :58); fluid boundaries dispatch-only under an omit-mask (:48); ac_composed_world_dump.py raising TypeError (:124); every NMII/FA/nucleus force scale a PI-GAP. The one that LOOKS architectural is CHEMICAL_FLUX: the family is declared (contracts.py:36) but 'no ConnectorContract in the 32 uses the family' (:62), awaiting the PI-gated 32->36 rewiring - still not an architecture gap for this question, since G-actin/water flux is a transport channel rather than a mechanical load path and the pairs it needs are already declared.
result.notes:
ADVERSARY VERDICT. The 13-COMPONENT set is complete - I could not construct a single structure of an adherent crawling MCF7-like cell that needs a 14th state owner. Every candidate resolves to (i) component-internal (chromatin/lamin, microvilli, crosslinkers, ECM damage, MTOC, membrane skeleton), (ii) an existing component instanced differently (substrate = ECM with far_field_dirichlet; contractile ring = equatorial NMII on cortex; spindle = MT topology; EMT keratin->vimentin = IF constitutive card, ac/solid/intermediate_filament.py:10-12), (iii) mechanically negligible (organelle passengers; extracellular medium at Re ~ 1e-13), (iv) a kinetic process (nucleation/severing/capping/MMP/adhesion turnover), or (v) out of scope with no second cell (cadherin, desmosome, tight junction). Both PI examples are expressible today: the crawl dipole closes front-to-rear through connectors 17/20/6/31 and 25/5/6, and ECM remodelling emerges from clutch pull + ecm_crosslink KMC + membrane steric push acting on ECM-internal damage/alignment state.

I applied one consistent architecture-level test, which is the strongest sufficiency argument available: since the graph "declares allowed component-level load paths" (contracts.py:188) and no component may touch another's state except through a registered connector (CELL_ENGINE_ARCHITECTURE.md:211), a load path is expressible-in-principle iff its component PAIR appears in the graph. Adding a second force law to an existing pair is an in-architecture extension - the tree already does exactly that (SURFACE_BODY_PLAN.md:219 adds a one-sided contact coupler to the membrane-cortex pair ERM already occupies). That test dissolves every candidate a critic will raise - MT plus-end end-stop (MT-cortex exists), cortex-to-FA (two series routes), membrane-to-FA (series via ERM), IF-to-substrate (3-hop series via plectin+FA; alpha6beta4's ligand is laminin, not collagen-I), lamellipodium-to-ECM (correctly routed through the interposed membrane) - except one.

THE ONE THING I COULD NOT ARGUE AWAY: the nucleus has NO component-level edge to the cell surface. Measured neighbours are exactly {cytosol, intermediate_filament, microtubule, sf_arc}; ('cortex','nucleus') and ('membrane','nucleus') are absent pairs, and the CONTACT family is instanced on only 3 pairs, none nuclear. So the largest and stiffest body in the cell can be loaded by the surface only through bilateral discrete LINC tethers (explicitly "NOT a steric term", ac/solid/INTEGRATION.md:92-93) and a pore pressure that drains in ~0.1-0.6 s (D_p 40-60 um^2/s, Moeendarbary 2013). Three in-tree facts make this architectural rather than a ladder rung: the nucleus mesh is retained specifically for "collision" with no consumer connector (FLUID_CORE_PLAN.md:21-22); the incumbent's single global steric channel marks nucleus nodes dormant so EV skips them (ac/cell/assemble.py:19-21, 812-820) - and even if it did not, a shared-array steric channel is the forbidden co-location mechanism; and the IF strut that historically carried nucleus<->cortex was deliberately re-routed to sf_arc (INTERMEDIATE_FILAMENT_PLAN.md:53-55) although the legacy module named it "the nucleus<->cortex load path that fixes the mechanically-DECOUPLED nucleus". The project's own native measurement is the observable: nucleus flattening 0.0% while the cortex deformed 751 nm, verdict "the interior is mechanically DECOUPLED from the cortex" (INTERNAL_DISPLACEMENT_DIAGNOSIS_2026-07-16.md:13-22). That 2026-07-16 diagnosis listed four fixes; the engine graph adopted A (cytosol pressure = connector 4) and D (LINC = 8/9/11), adopted B only partially (IF exists but its cortex anchor was dropped), and never adopted C (MT engagement). The remaining hole is the DIRECT bearing edge.

Cost of the fix - why the verdict is SUFFICIENT_WITH_CAVEATS rather than GAPS_FOUND: zero new components, two CONTACT connectors (32 -> 34), with the force law, the force-free-at-physiological-gap semantics, and the "collision must not manufacture adhesion" separation already written down for the membrane-cortex pair. Severity is BLOCKS_DEFORMATION_COUPLING, not BLOCKS_CRAWL: 2D crawling still works without it; what fails is the cortex deforming the nucleus and the nucleus stopping a crumpling cortex - precisely PI priority (i) - and it becomes BLOCKS_CRAWL as soon as migration is through 3D collagen pores where nuclear deformation is rate-limiting (Wolf 2013, JCB 201:1069).

gaps.structure: Plectin cytolinker anchor of the intermediate-filament network to CORTICAL F-actin (and to the membrane cytoskeleton) — the peripheral end of the keratin/vimentin cage
gaps.connects: intermediate_filament <-> cortex (secondarily intermediate_filament <-> membrane)
gaps.why_architecture_cannot_express_it: The connector graph is the closed, exhaustive enumeration of legal inter-component load paths: `CELL_ENGINE_ARCHITECTURE.md:211` — "no component can mutate another component's state except through a registered connector/coupler" — and `contracts.py:129-142` validates that every load path is a declared (component_a, component_b) pair. `intermediate_filament`'s declared neighbours are exactly {nucleus, sf_arc, cytosol} (`contracts.py:310-322, 339-343`). The ONLY IF-to-actin edge is `if_sf_plectin` = IF<->sf_arc (`contracts.py:317-322`). So an IF filament can only reach the cell surface WHERE A STRESS FIBER EXISTS. This is not an unimplemented edge — it is a prohibited one, and it was prohibited deliberately: `INTERMEDIATE_FILAMENT_PLAN.md:53-55` lists the cortex anchor under "Missing or structurally invalid" and rules that the legacy nearest-cortex spring must be replaced by "an SF/arc plectin endpoint". Meanwhile the code on disk requires the edge the graph forbids: `ac/solid/intermediate_filament.py:3-7` builds "the nucleus<->cortex load path that fixes the mechanically-DECOUPLED nucleus" with "cortex anchor (spoke outer bead <-> cortex)"; `ac/engine/intermediate_filament_rig.py:650-651` states "LINC, cortex anchor, and internal crosslinks are NOT here (graph- and component-crosslink-owned)" — the rig correctly hands the cortex anchor to the graph, and the graph has nowhere to put it (`intermediate_filament_rig.py:625-633` hard-rejects any cage that carries it component-locally).
gaps.observable_that_would_be_wrong: (1) IF cannot act as a load-bearing third tension net anywhere without a ventral stress fiber — i.e. over the entire dorsal/apical cortex, and in any rounded or SF-poor state the whole IF network is mechanically dangling (only anchors: nuclear envelope + cytosol drag). An IF-ablation A/B on whole-cell/cortical stiffness would return ~0 change, contradicting keratin knockdown softening epithelial cells 30-60% (Seltmann et al. 2013 PNAS 110:18507, 10.1073/pnas.1310493110 — the project's own citation at `ac/solid/intermediate_filament.py:13`). (2) Cortical/cell-surface load cannot reach the perinuclear IF cage, so the vimentin/keratin nuclear-protection safety net (Patteson et al. 2019 JCB 218:4079, 10.1083/jcb.201902046, cited at `ac/solid/intermediate_filament.py:15`) cannot emerge. (3) Directly measurable in the engine: the isolated-cage gate at `ac/solid/intermediate_filament.py:22-23` ("displacing the cortex anchors transmits a nonzero force to the nucleus beads") has NO composed-graph equivalent — displace the cortex in the composed cell and the nucleus feels nothing except via sf_arc.

The incumbent `ac/cell` has the same hole: the global WCA excludes nucleus and membrane nodes by construction (`ac/cell/assemble.py:813-820`, "non-actin blocks get distinct ids AND active<0 (skip EV)" / "<0 dormant -> EV skips myosin/nucleus/membrane"), and `LINC_CONNECTOR_PLAN.md:236` orders the one remaining incumbent nucleus-cortex spring DISABLED for the new engine with no replacement edge declared.
gaps.observable_that_would_be_wrong: (1) Nuclear flattening on spreading: nuclear height/aspect would be set only by actin-cap LINC tethers plus a smooth poroelastic pressure field, with no geometric limit imposed by the cell's own basal and apical surfaces; under `actin_cap_linc` contraction (contracts.py:290-296) there is literally no reaction force available to stop the nucleus, so it can be driven THROUGH the basal cortex and out through the membrane. This is a hard, cheap-to-check invariant (max nuclear-node penetration depth past the cortex/membrane surface) and it will be violated. Reference: Khatau et al. 2009 PNAS 106:19017, 10.1073/pnas.0908686106 (perinuclear actin cap compresses the nucleus and sets nuclear shape). (2) The nuclear-piston mode of forward movement cannot form: pressure compartmentalization requires the nucleus to seal against the cortex to partition fore/aft cytoplasm. The project's own KB note on this source says it is exactly "a nucleus<->cortex load path" (Petrie, Koo & Yamada 2014 Science 345:1062, 10.1126/science.1256965; KB citation_key Petrie2014_Science, source_audit verdict=OK). (3) Confinement-driven nuclear-envelope strain cannot arise from cell-shape change, so the nuclear-ruler feedback eps_NE -> cPLA2 -> myosin II -> cortical tension cannot close (Lomakin et al. 2020 Science, 10.1126/science.aba2894; KB Lomakin2020_Science verdict=OK -> KB-1.17, whose own `assumptions` field reads "nucleus also a mechanical obstacle (KU-1.8)").
gaps.evidence: Measured adjacency of `nucleus` = {cytosol, intermediate_filament, microtubule, sf_arc}; ffn_sim/ac/engine/contracts.py:268-272 (FLUID_BOUNDARY, kinetics=False), :344-350, :371-377, :445-450 (CONTACT used only on other pairs); ffn_sim/ac/engine/ecm_world.py:937-949 (CONTACT runtime template already exists); ffn_sim/docs/v2_audit/cell_engine/SURFACE_BODY_PLAN.md:219; ffn_sim/ac/cell/assemble.py:813-820; ffn_sim/docs/v2_audit/cell_engine/LINC_CONNECTOR_PLAN.md:236; ffn_sim/docs/v2_audit/cell_engine/CELL_ENGINE_ARCHITECTURE.md:211; KB source_evidence Petrie2014_Science (10.1126/science.1256965, verdict OK) and Lomakin2020_Science (10.1126/science.aba2894, verdict OK) -> knowledge_claim KB-1.17; ffn_sim/docs/ACTIN_ARCHITECTURE_NOTES.md:391-396 (the project's own migration-mode map lists "lobopodial ... hydrostatic pressure + nuclear pistoning"). Grep confirms zero occurrences of `nucleus_cortex` / `nucleus_membrane` anywhere in the tree.
gaps.proposed_fix: Add two CONTACT connectors modelled exactly on `membrane_ecm_contact` (contracts.py:445-450): `nucleus_cortex_contact` (nucleus <-> cortex) and `nucleus_membrane_contact` (nucleus <-> membrane), both `ConnectorFamily.CONTACT, kinetics=False, commit_on_accept=False, generation_required=True, remap_on_accept=True, blocks_sleep_refine=True`, one-sided short-range repulsion that is force-free at the physiological gap so the physiological baseline starts at zero contact force. Reuse the `ecm_world.py:937-949` validation shape and the SURFACE_BODY_PLAN.md:219 membrane-cortex contact law. 32 -> 34.

gaps.structure: Plectin/cytolinker cross-bridge between the intermediate-filament network and microtubules (the lateral reinforcement that lets MTs carry compression, and the IF template for MT organisation)
gaps.connects: intermediate_filament <-> microtubule
gaps.why_architecture_cannot_express_it: `microtubule`'s declared neighbours are {nucleus, cortex, sf_arc, cytosol} (contracts.py:297-309, :323-328, :334-338) and `intermediate_filament`'s are {nucleus, sf_arc, cytosol}. The pair is undeclared, therefore prohibited per CELL_ENGINE_ARCHITECTURE.md:211. The graph HAS the sibling edge for the other filament system — `mt_sf_spectraplakin` (MT <-> sf_arc, contracts.py:323-328) — so the omission is specific to IF, not to cytolinkers in general. The project's own KB draft row asserts the edge: KB-DRAFT-3.B-10 "Cytolinker crosslinks with correct identity (plectin IF-IF, IF-actin, **IF-MT**)".
gaps.observable_that_would_be_wrong: MT compressive load capacity. Without lateral reinforcement from the surrounding IF/cytoskeletal network, a microtubule's critical buckling load is the free Euler value F = pi^2 kappa / L^2, ~2 orders of magnitude below the load MTs actually bear in living cells; buckling appears as long-wavelength single-arc modes instead of the observed short-wavelength reinforced modes (Brangwynne et al. 2006 J Cell Biol 173:733, 10.1083/jcb.200601060). In the graph, MT compression can only be reacted at `mt_cortex_capture`, `mt_nucleus_linc` and `mt_sf_spectraplakin`, so the MT strut array of the tensegrity picture will buckle at the wrong load and wrong wavelength. Second observable: loss of the IF template for MT network organisation, i.e. no mechanism for persistent polarity in directed migration (Gan et al. 2016 Cell Systems 3:252, 10.1016/j.cels.2016.08.007).
gaps.evidence: Measured adjacency: microtubule = {cortex, cytosol, nucleus, sf_arc}, intermediate_filament = {cytosol, nucleus, sf_arc} — pair absent; ffn_sim/ac/engine/contracts.py:297-328; ffn_sim/docs/v2_audit/cell_engine/CELL_ENGINE_ARCHITECTURE.md:211; project KB knowledge_claim KB-DRAFT-3.B-10 ("plectin IF-IF, IF-actin, IF-MT"); KB source_evidence Svitkina1996 = Svitkina, Verkhovsky & Borisy 1996 J Cell Biol 135:991, 10.1083/jcb.135.4.991, title "Plectin sidearms mediate interaction of intermediate filaments with **microtubules** and other components of the cytoskeleton" (source_audit verdict=CHECK, i.e. metadata-drift class, not fabrication); Brangwynne et al. 2006 10.1083/jcb.200601060; Gan et al. 2016 10.1016/j.cels.2016.08.007.
gaps.proposed_fix: Add `if_mt_plectin` (ConnectorFamily.PLECTIN, intermediate_filament <-> microtubule, kinetics=True, commit_on_accept=True, chemistry_card="plectin_if_microtubule"), structurally identical to `if_sf_plectin`/`mt_sf_spectraplakin`. Land it with `if_cortex_plectin` in the same contract change (both are the same PLECTIN family and the same rate card family).

gaps.structure: Direct intermediate-filament anchorage to a matrix adhesion — plectin-1f-mediated IF attachment at focal adhesions (the non-hemidesmosomal IF-to-substrate load path)
gaps.connects: intermediate_filament <-> focal_adhesion (and thence to ecm via the existing integrin_collagen_clutch)
gaps.why_architecture_cannot_express_it: `focal_adhesion`'s declared neighbours are {sf_arc, ecm, lamellipodium, filopodium} (contracts.py:273-283, :364-370, :391-397). The IF network's only route to the substrate is intermediate_filament -> sf_arc (if_sf_plectin) -> focal_adhesion (fa_actin_anchor) -> ecm, i.e. strictly in series with a stress fiber. A plectin-1f-anchored IF terminating AT the adhesion plaque is in series with the integrin, in PARALLEL with the actin path — mechanically a different topology, and the graph cannot draw it. Direct answer to the audit question about hemidesmosomes: for interphase luminal MCF7 on collagen I the HEMIDESMOSOMAL version (keratin-plectin-1a-alpha6beta4-laminin-332) is correctly absent — no laminin-332 ligand on a collagen-I substrate, and the project's own KB records that MCF7 lacks alpha6beta4 (KB-PIV-5, `ffn_sim/docs/PI_EXP_VALIDATION_MAP.md:93-94` "MCF7 lacks alpha6beta4 (so no alpha6beta4-keratin mechanoprotection)"; `COMPARTMENT_BUILD_PLAN_2026-07-07.md:6` excludes desmosome/hemidesmosome by design). What is NOT covered by that exclusion is the plectin-1f/FA route, which is laminin- and beta4-independent and becomes the dominant IF-substrate load path exactly when vimentin comes up.
gaps.observable_that_would_be_wrong: For the named later target (EMT progression): after the keratin->vimentin switch, the IF network cannot bear or modulate substrate traction at all. Observables that would be wrong: FA size/turnover and total traction change on plectin or vimentin perturbation (Gregor et al. 2014 FASEB J 28:715, 10.1096/fj.13-231829 "Mechanosensing through focal adhesion-anchored intermediate filaments"; Burgstaller, Gregor, Winter & Wiche 2010 Mol Biol Cell 21:3362, 10.1091/mbc.E10-02-0094); and IF-mediated restriction of traction force (De Pascalis et al. 2018 J Cell Biol 217:3031, 10.1083/jcb.201801162). For the CURRENT target (interphase MCF7 on collagen) the error is small — this is why the severity is magnitude-only, not blocking.
gaps.evidence: Measured adjacency: focal_adhesion = {ecm, filopodium, lamellipodium, sf_arc}; intermediate_filament = {cytosol, nucleus, sf_arc}; ffn_sim/ac/engine/contracts.py:273-283, 310-322, 364-370, 391-397; MCF7 alpha6beta4 exclusion: ffn_sim/docs/PI_EXP_VALIDATION_MAP.md:93-94 and ffn_sim/docs/v2_audit/COMPARTMENT_BUILD_PLAN_2026-07-07.md:6 (KB-PIV-5); ffn_sim/docs/v2_audit/FILAMENT_SUBSYSTEM_PLAN_2026-07-16.md:177 (project's own epithelial anchor topology table: "desmosome (cell-cell) + hemidesmosome"); EMT-side literature 10.1096/fj.13-231829, 10.1091/mbc.E10-02-0094, 10.1083/jcb.201801162 — NOTE: none of these three are in the project KB (source_evidence returns nothing for Gregor/Burgstaller/plectin-1f), so they are PI-registration candidates, not yet KB-anchored.
gaps.proposed_fix: Do NOT add a hemidesmosome. Add one connector `if_fa_plectin` (ConnectorFamily.PLECTIN, intermediate_filament <-> focal_adhesion, kinetics=True, commit_on_accept=True, chemistry_card="plectin1f_if_adhesion") gated OFF (zero population) for the keratin/luminal-MCF7 cell card and turned on with the vimentin card, so the EMT switch is a population change on a declared edge rather than a future contract change. Register the three sources above as SourceEvidence first.

gaps.structure: Extracellular / interstitial fluid — the Biot-Darcy pore-pressure field of the hydrated collagen ECM, and the external reservoir on the far side of the semipermeable membrane
gaps.connects: ecm <-> interstitial fluid (and membrane <-> extracellular fluid for transmembrane water flux)
gaps.why_architecture_cannot_express_it: There is no fluid component outside the cell. `cytosol` is declared "Biot/Darcy finite-volume field" and is INTRAcellular — its neighbours are the intracellular components plus the membrane/nucleus fluid boundaries (contracts.py:208, 258-272, 329-343, 358-363, 386-390). `ecm` is declared "fiber/crosslink world" (contracts.py:243-245) with neighbours {focal_adhesion, membrane, world_boundary, ecm} — no fluid edge exists or can exist. `ecm_far_field_anchor` is `kinetics=False, commit_on_accept=False` (contracts.py:439-444), i.e. a non-dissipative elastic tie to a reference frame, not a drainage boundary. So the ECM has a solid skeleton with no pore pressure and the membrane's water flux has no external reservoir.
gaps.observable_that_would_be_wrong: (1) The time-dependence of how the cell deforms and remodels the collagen it pulls on. A hydrated collagen gel's dominant short-time load path in compression is the interstitial fluid, not the fiber skeleton (Chandran & Barocas 2004 J Biomech Eng 126:152, 10.1115/1.1688774); without it the ECM response is instantaneous-elastic plus fiber plasticity only, so cell-on-gel stress relaxation and the spatial decay of the traction-induced displacement field are mis-timed. The project already inventoried exactly this: the KB row for this source states it "unblocks: ECM interstitial fluid / poroelastic (Biot-Darcy) pore-pressure field p(x,t) - solid collagen skeleton coupled to Darcy [Compartment 10 - ECM ...]". (2) The osmotic-engine / water-permeation mode of migration cannot be expressed at all, since transmembrane water has nowhere to go (Stroka et al. 2014 Cell 157:611, 10.1016/j.cell.2014.02.052).
gaps.evidence: Measured adjacency: ecm = {ecm, focal_adhesion, membrane, world_boundary}; cytosol = intracellular set only; ffn_sim/ac/engine/contracts.py:208, 243-250, 258-272, 439-444; grep for interstitial/poroelastic/drained in ffn_sim/ac/engine/ecm_world.py and ecm_mechanics.py returns zero hits; KB source_evidence Chandran2004 = 10.1115/1.1688774, notes field naming the ECM-interstitial-fluid compartment as the thing it unblocks (source_audit verdict=CHECK); Stroka et al. 2014 10.1016/j.cell.2014.02.052 (not in project KB).
gaps.proposed_fix: Two acceptable resolutions, and the PI should pick one explicitly rather than leaving it implicit: (a) minimum — record a contract decision that the extracellular space is an infinite ambient-pressure bath, i.e. a constant-pressure Dirichlet BC carried inside `membrane` and `ecm`, which is defensible for 2D crawling on collagen in a large medium volume and consistent with the ratified constant-Pi_0 = 40 Pa turgor decision; or (b) full — add a 14th component `extracellular_fluid` (ComponentRole.FLUID_VOLUME, Biot/Darcy) with `ecm_interstitial_transfer` (IMMERSED_TRANSFER, ecm <-> extracellular_fluid) and `membrane_extracellular_boundary` (FLUID_BOUNDARY, membrane <-> extracellular_fluid), needed before any confined-migration or 3D-gel target. Option (a) is sufficient for the current adherent-crawl goal; do not silently rely on it.

confirmed_sufficient: CORTEX AS ONE CONNECTED, CRUMPLING OBJECT (the PI's observable (i)) — expressible. `cortex` is a single state-owning component, "explicit crosslinked F-actin network" (contracts.py:202-206), so intra-cortical crosslinks and self-contact are legitimately component-internal (per the audit's stated exclusions plus `ac/cell/assemble.py:939-943` StericForce WCA over actin nodes with same-filament exclusion). Nothing in the architecture forces the cortex to be label-blind or to share nodes; the disjoint-population invariant is what makes it one object rather than a merged array.

LAMELLIPODIUM -> ECM REMODELLING -> FORWARD MOVEMENT (the PI's observable (ii)) — the entire load path is expressible with no missing edge. Protrusion: `lamellipodium_membrane_contact` CONTACT, chemistry `actin_membrane_brownian_ratchet_contact` (contracts.py:344-350). Grip: `lamellipodium_nascent_fa` (:364-370) -> `integrin_collagen_clutch` (:278-283, generation_required + remap_on_accept + blocks_sleep_refine). Mechanical ECM remodelling: `ecm_crosslink` is INTERNAL, kinetic, remap_on_accept (:433-438) = fiber realignment + crosslink rupture = plastic densification; reaction closes at `ecm_far_field_anchor` -> `world_boundary` (:439-444). Cell-body advance and rear release: `nmii_cortex_motor`/`nmii_sf_motor` (:405-411, :398-404) -> cortex/sf_arc -> `sf_cortex_transient` (:284-289) -> `fa_actin_anchor` (:273-277) -> clutch rupture. Both the front (nascent) and rear (mature) adhesion classes are separately declared.

STRESS-FIBER SUBTYPES — ventral, dorsal, transverse arc and perinuclear cap are all inside `sf_arc` with the correct topology rules: `dorsal_arc_crosslink` as an INTERNAL sf_arc<->sf_arc connector (contracts.py:428-432), `actin_cap_linc` as the cap-to-nucleus edge (:290-296), and `LOAD_PATH_PLAN.md:100-107` explicitly FORBIDS the wrong ones (transverse arc -> FA direct; whole SF welded to cortex).
FILOPODIUM — full set: tip contact (:371-377), root coupling with fascin/formin chemistry (:378-384), cytosol/G-actin transfer (:385-390), nascent FA (:391-397), NMII (:420-427).

MICROTUBULES AS A LOAD PATH — the compression-strut path is complete and correctly typed: `mt_cortex_capture` is ConnectorFamily.MOTOR with chemistry `microtubule_cortical_dynein` (:304-309), `mt_nucleus_linc` endpoint role is "plus-end or motor-bound lattice site" (:297-303), plus `mt_sf_spectraplakin` (:323-328) and `mt_cytosol_transfer` (:334-338). Dynein/kinesin CARGO transport is not a cell-scale load path and is correctly not a connector. The centrosome/MTOC is legitimately a junction node inside the "dynamic rod graph" representation (:222-224), and its load reaches the nucleus through `mt_nucleus_linc`.

IF CELL-TYPE IDENTITY (keratin K8/K18 vs vimentin, the EMT switch) — correctly a component-internal constitutive preset, not a component: `ac/engine/intermediate_filament_rig.py:62-79`, `ac/solid/intermediate_filament.py:47-49`, KB-3.26. Only the modulus/persistence-length differs; geometry and kernel are shared.

ADHESION CLASSES — nascent (lamellipodium/filopodium), mature (sf_arc), and fibrillar are one FA_CLUTCH/ACTIN_ANCHOR family differing only by chemistry_card and maturation state inside the "stochastic clutch graph" (:218-221). The two-stage series joint is correctly declared as ONE composite mechanical joint via `mechanical_group="alpha2beta1_collagen_series"` (:273-283) and deduplicated at bind time (`composition.py:17-20`) so it is never a spring-in-series double count. Substituting fibronectin/alpha5beta1 is a chemistry_card change, not an architecture change.

MEMBRANE — bilayer Helfrich surface (:199-201); area reservoir/microvilli/ruffles component-internal (per audit exclusions); glycocalyx is a modifier of the `membrane_ecm_contact` potential (:445-450) and of the clutch, not a component; caveolae are correctly irrelevant for MCF7 (Cav-1-negative). Membrane<->cortex interpenetration is already specified as a one-sided contact term inside the surface solve (SURFACE_BODY_PLAN.md:219), and the SurfaceAnchor port mechanism (SURFACE_BODY_PLAN.md:230-243) lets any component attach to membrane or cortex without a permanent weld.

SPECTRIN/ANKYRIN MEMBRANE SKELETON AND SEPTINS — no new component or edge needed: these are additional linker families on the already-declared membrane<->cortex edge (a second connector with a different chemistry_card) or component-internal to `membrane`. The architecture permits multiple connectors per component pair.

NUCLEUS INTERNALS — envelope, lamina (lamin-A/C + lamin-B split), chromatin and nucleoli are correctly component-internal to "native lamina/chromatin FEM" (:210-214, forces_manifest.py:416-433); all three LINC classes are declared as separate typed edges (actin/sf_arc :290-296, MT :297-303, IF :310-316) rather than one lumped nucleoskeletal tie.

ORGANELLES (ER, mitochondria, Golgi, lipid droplets) — honestly assessed as mechanical passengers at whole-cell scale. Their contribution is crowding/inclusion stiffening of the cytoplasm, which is exactly the poroelastic storage + permeability the `cytosol` Biot/Darcy component owns (:208; Moeendarbary et al. 2013 Nat Mater 12:253, 10.1038/nmat3517 — cytoplasm behaves as a poroelastic material with a mesh size set by macromolecules and organelles). ER-microtubule coupling determines ER morphology, not cell shape. No component or connector is warranted.

CYTOPLASM — cytosol, poroelastic pore fluid and G-actin field are one component (:208) with adjoint IMMERSED_TRANSFER couplers to cortex, sf_arc, MT, IF, lamellipodium and filopodium (:258-262, :329-343, :358-363, :385-390) plus moving fluid boundaries at membrane and nuclear envelope (:263-272).

CORTEX -> FOCAL ADHESION — deliberately and defensibly indirect, not a gap: cortical load reaches the substrate as cortex -> `sf_cortex_transient` -> sf_arc -> `fa_actin_anchor` -> `integrin_collagen_clutch`, or cortex -> `lamellipodium_cortex_seam` -> lamellipodium -> `lamellipodium_nascent_fa`. `LOAD_PATH_PLAN.md:342` states the design intent: an open load path must report its unbalanced reaction and "the missing reaction is not reassigned to cortex". A 2-hop path exists, so the graph CAN express it.

CELL-CELL STRUCTURES (adherens-junction/E-cadherin belt, desmosomes, tight junctions, the apical actin ring) — correctly out of scope for a SINGLE cell; they have no partner surface to load against. Already documented as such at `NEW_ENGINE_BUILD_PLAN_2026-07-16.md:327-330` ("in ONE cell the desmosome (cell-cell) keratin anchoring has no ...") and `COMPARTMENT_BUILD_PLAN_2026-07-07.md:6`. Flagged only as a future-scope note for the EMT target, not a gap in the single-cell architecture.

CONTRACTILE RING / cytokinetic actin — mitotic; the PI's stated cell-cycle target is interphase, so its absence is scope, not a gap. When needed it is a cortex-internal ring-condensation mechanism plus existing NMII motor edges, not a new component.

ENDOCYTIC ACTIN — not a cell-scale load path (~100 nm, single-pit forces; the project's own reading note at ACTIN_ARCHITECTURE_NOTES.md:459-465 classifies the Serwas/Drubin cryo-ET endocytic network as "tangential" to cortex architecture). Correctly absent.
result.notes:
VERDICT SHAPE. The 13/32 graph is much closer to complete than I expected: both structures the PI named by hand are fully expressible with no missing edge (see confirmed_sufficient items 1-2). The gaps cluster in exactly one place — the third cytoskeletal net. `intermediate_filament` is the only filament component whose peripheral end has no surface edge, and `nucleus` is the only interior body with no contact edge. Gaps 1 and 2 are the same physical hole seen from two sides: THE NUCLEUS HAS NO MECHANICAL RELATIONSHIP WITH THE CELL SURFACE except through a stress fiber. Fixing them is 3 connectors (32 -> 35), all of which are structural clones of connectors that already exist (`if_sf_plectin`, `membrane_ecm_contact`), and one of which (`if_cortex_plectin`) already has orphaned runtime bonds waiting for it in `intermediate_filament_rig.py`. I would land those three as one contract change before anything else on this list.

STRONGEST SINGLE PIECE OF EVIDENCE, and the reason I rate Gap 1 as blocking rather than cosmetic: `ffn_sim/ac/engine/intermediate_filament_rig.py:650-651` says the cortex-anchor bonds are "graph- ... owned" and `:625-633` hard-raises if a cage tries to carry them component-locally. The engine has correctly delegated a load path to a connector that does not exist. That is a true architecture defect, not an implementation backlog item, and it was created by an explicit ruling (`INTERMEDIATE_FILAMENT_PLAN.md:53-55`) that re-points the cortex anchor at `sf_arc` — a modelling decision I believe is biologically wrong and that the PI should be asked to reverse. Combined with `LINC_CONNECTOR_PLAN.md:236` (disable the incumbent's nearest-cortex spring), the net effect of the current plan of record is to REMOVE the last nucleus<->cortex load path from the running code without declaring a replacement edge — while `ac/solid/intermediate_filament.py:3-4` says that path is what "fixes the mechanically-DECOUPLED nucleus".

THINGS I CHECKED AND DECIDED ARE **NOT** ARCHITECTURE GAPS, recorded so they are not re-litigated:
- `membrane <-> focal_adhesion`. Integrin is transmembrane, so the plasma membrane is physically pinned at every adhesion, and membrane tension is partly borne there. But the dominant force path is actin-talin-integrin-ECM, which bypasses the bilayer; the residual (membrane immobilisation at the plaque, enforcement of the ~30 nm basal gap) is a second-order constraint that the existing `membrane_ecm_contact` + ERM edges approximate. COSMETIC. Worth one sentence in the architecture doc rather than an edge.
- `microtubule <-> focal_adhesion`. Real and important for crawling — MT targeting triggers FA disassembly (Kaverina, Krylyshkina & Small 1999 J Cell Biol 146:1033, 10.1083/jcb.146.5.1033) — but it is a REGULATORY/kinetic coupling, not a load path: the MT does not carry the substrate load. Under the audit's stated standard it does not qualify. It does, however, mean rear-adhesion disassembly in the composed cell must come from clutch force-dependent kinetics alone. Flag to PI as a scope question, not an architecture gap.
- `lamellipodium <-> sf_arc`. Transverse arcs and dorsal SFs are born from the lamellipodial network (Hotulainen & Lappalainen 2006 J Cell Biol 173:383, 10.1083/jcb.200511093; Burnette et al. 2011 Nat Cell Biol 13:371, 10.1038/ncb2205). Mechanically there IS a 2-hop path (lamellipodium -> `lamellipodium_cortex_seam` -> cortex -> `sf_cortex_transient` -> sf_arc) and a load path through the shared FA, so the graph can express it. What it cannot express is a *filament identity transfer* from lamellipodium to sf_arc — but that is a PopulationLedger/topology operation under the disjoint-population invariant, not a connector, and is correctly not a connector.
- `membrane/cortex <-> world_boundary`. `world_boundary` is declared `owns_geometry=False, dynamically_evolving=False` (contracts.py:246-250), i.e. a reference frame, not a surface, so there is no rigid dish plane. For a collagen coating dense enough that `membrane_ecm_contact` provides continuous basal support this is fine; for a sparse fiber ECM the cell has no basal floor. Worth a config-level assertion (basal contact coverage) rather than a new edge.
- IF-to-ECM via HEMIDESMOSOME specifically: correctly absent for MCF7 on collagen I. See gap 4's rationale — no laminin-332 ligand, and MCF7 lacks alpha6beta4 per the project's own KB-PIV-5. I report only the plectin-1f/FA route, at magnitude-only severity, and only because EMT is a named later target.

TWO ADJACENT ITEMS THAT ARE NOT LOAD PATHS BUT WILL BITE THE CRAWL TARGET (reported here rather than as gaps, since the standard is force transmission):
1. `ConnectorFamily.CHEMICAL_FLUX` is declared (contracts.py:36) and has a full 5-kernel runtime (`ac/engine/monomer_flux.py`), but ZERO of the 32 connectors use it — independently confirmed by `AUDIT_AC_ENGINE_2026-07-25.md:60`. The G-actin endpoint role appears only on the lamellipodium/filopodium IMMERSED_TRANSFER edges ("porous drag and G-actin transport stencil", contracts.py:358-363, 385-390); the cortex and sf_arc transfer edges carry porous fluid only ("porous-fluid transfer stencil", :258-262, :329-333). So cortex and stress fibers cannot draw from or return to the shared monomer pool: no cortical treadmilling, no monomer competition between compartments, and protrusion mass balance is unconserved across the cell. This is a MASS path, and it is already documented as the PI-pending 32 -> 36 rewiring (`CYTOSOL_CONNECTED_AND_GACTIN_FLUX_2026-07-23.md:68-75`). Recommend closing it in the same contract change as gaps 1-3, since the PI signature is already queued.
2. Proteolytic ECM remodelling (MT1-MMP/MMP14 fiber scission at the cell surface) has no path: `membrane_ecm_contact` is `kinetics=False, commit_on_accept=False, chemistry_card=None` (contracts.py:445-450), so the cell can push and pull collagen but cannot cut it. For the PI's "remodels the ECM" observable in 2D this is fine — 2D mesenchymal crawling on collagen is largely MMP-independent and the mechanical remodelling channel (`ecm_crosslink` rupture + fiber realignment) is present and correctly kinetic. It becomes a hard requirement for 3D invasion, which the project's own KB already anticipates (KB-1.8: "Below threshold MMP proteolysis required").

CITATION HYGIENE. gaps.structure: Nucleus↔cortex / nucleus↔membrane steric-contact (compressive, non-penetrating) joint — the mechanical abutment between the nuclear envelope and the enclosing cortical shell / plasma membrane
gaps.connects: component `nucleus` (CORE_BODY) ↔ components `cortex` and `membrane` (SURFACE_BODY)
gaps.why_architecture_cannot_express_it: In the 32, `nucleus` has exactly four edges: `nucleus_cytosol_boundary` (FLUID_BOUNDARY, isotropic/normal pressure traction) and three LINC edges to `sf_arc`/`microtubule`/`intermediate_filament` (contracts.py:268-272, 290-316). `neighbors('nucleus')` = {cytosol, intermediate_filament, microtubule, sf_arc} — there is NO edge to cortex or membrane at all, and no CONTACT-family instance anywhere in the cell interior (the CONTACT family is instantiated only on lamellipodium–membrane :344-350, filopodium–membrane :371-377, membrane–ECM :445-450). The architecture forbids routing it any other way: 'no component can mutate another component's state except through a registered connector/coupler' (CELL_ENGINE_ARCHITECTURE.md:211) and 'Concatenating two components into one array is not a connection' (:109-110), so a global label-blind exclusion kernel like the incumbent's all-fiber WCA (forces_manifest.py:260-262) is inadmissible in the engine. The one legacy direct nucleus–cortex edge was deliberately retired without a contact replacement (FLUID_CORE_PLAN.md:112-114 §3.3 '새 경로에서 폐기: nucleus↔nearest-cortex 정적 LINC pairing'), and the plan's coupling table (:296-303) lists nucleus↔cytosol + SF/MT/IF↔nucleus as the complete set.
gaps.observable_that_would_be_wrong: (a) Interpenetration: a crumpling/indented cortex or an inward-pushed membrane passes THROUGH the nuclear envelope instead of being stopped by it — this exact failure is already on record as the S3 'nucleus pokes through the cortex' artifact (SINGLE_CELL_BUILDUP_PLAN_2026-07-16.md:78, 84), and it was patched with a LINC spring, not with an exclusion law. (b) Nuclear steric arrest is unmeasurable: KB-3.B2.3 (verified) states 'Nucleus = rate-limiting steric element', physical arrest at ~10% of undeformed cross-section, tumour critical cross-section ≈7 µm² (Wolf2013_JCB, verdict OK, 10.1083/jcb.201210152) — the framework itself calls the nucleus 'the largest steric bottleneck in pore transit' (CELL_MECHANICS_FRAMEWORK_2026-07-15.md:110). With only isotropic-ish pore pressure plus sparse LINC bonds, the nucleus cannot be squeezed by the confining boundary, so pore-transit arrest, nuclear flattening by the actin cap pressing on the envelope, and envelope-rupture-by-confinement (DenaisRaab2016_Science, verdict OK) come out wrong or absent. (c) An adherent cell cannot flatten its nucleus against the substrate by cortical compression.

This is a documented REPLACEMENT of a working edge, not an omission: the landed module is explicitly a nucleus↔cortex load path with cortex-anchor bonds and a passing coupling gate ('displacing the cortex anchors transmits a nonzero force to the nucleus beads … the isolated-cage test asserts the nucleus feels the cortex', ac/solid/intermediate_filament.py:3-7, 22-23), and the engine plan rejects it: 'The cortex anchor is not the registered composition. The common engine graph declares if_nucleus_linc and if_sf_plectin; the legacy wrapper hard-wires a nearest-cortex spring instead of an SF/arc plectin endpoint' (INTERMEDIATE_FILAMENT_PLAN.md:53-55, cf. :40 which counts the legacy cortical-anchor bonds).

Without a peripheral anchor the ablation delta is ~0 wherever SFs are sparse: a locally over-strained cortex/membrane patch has no IF safety net to shunt load into, so cortical rupture/bleb-nucleation thresholds are too low and the keratin(MCF7)↔vimentin(post-EMT) mechanical contrast — the whole point of KB-3.26/3.27 and of the EMT target — has no surface-load observable to move. Also, MT lateral reinforcement by vimentin is not expressible at all (no IF↔MT edge), and vimentin/plectin load-bearing at adhesions cannot reach the substrate.

confirmed_sufficient: CRAWL CIRCUIT CLOSES END-TO-END. The full protrusion→traction→translation→retraction loop is expressible with no missing edge: lamellipodium polymerizes against the membrane (17 `lamellipodium_membrane_contact`, Brownian-ratchet chemistry card) → nascent adhesion (20) → composite α2β1 clutch (5+6, one `alpha2beta1_collagen_series` mechanical group) → collagen ECM (30 internal crosslink KMC, kinetic + generation_required + remap_on_accept) → far-field reaction (31 `ecm_far_field_anchor` → world_boundary); cell body follows via the lamellipodium rear seam (18) and cortex NMII (26) → SF transient coupling (7) → FA (5); rear release is the same clutch's force-dependent unbind. contracts.py:344-370, 273-283, 433-444.

ECM REMODELLING BY A PROTRUSION IS EXPRESSIBLE (PI example ii). `ecm_crosslink` is kinetic/commit-on-accept with generation_required + remap_on_accept + blocks_sleep_refine (contracts.py:433-438), and ECM component-internal state is declared as 'alignment, crosslink, damage/remodelling' (CELL_ENGINE_ARCHITECTURE.md:71); `ecm_far_field_anchor` gives the reaction a ground and `membrane_ecm_contact` gives fiber-vs-cell steric. Plastic densification/alignment and proteolytic damage therefore have a home.

CORTEX AS ONE CRUMPLING OBJECT (PI example i) IS A COMPONENT-INTERNAL QUESTION, and the architecture is right about it: cortex owns 'filament IDs, crosslinks, NMII, turnover' internally (CELL_ENGINE_ARCHITECTURE.md:61), so its connectivity/percolation and its own self-contact are internal state, not connectors. No extra component or connector is needed for cortex integrity (see gap #3 for what it hits once it crumples).

THE PI 10-COMPARTMENT SPEC MAPS 1:1 ONTO THE 13 WITH EXACTLY ONE GAP. membrane→`membrane`; actin cortex→`cortex`; internal cytoskeleton→`sf_arc`+`lamellipodium`+`filopodium`+`microtubule`+`intermediate_filament`; myosin+crosslinkers→`nmii` + connectors 25-30 + internal KMC; cytoplasm→`cytosol`; nucleus→`nucleus` + LINC 8/9/11; volume/osmotic→distributed (see next item); cell–ECM clutch→`focal_adhesion`+5/6; cell–cell junction→ABSENT (gap #4); ECM→`ecm`+30/31/32. (CELL_MECHANICS_FRAMEWORK_2026-07-15.md:71-133 vs contracts.py:198-452.)

THE OSMOTIC/VOLUME COMPARTMENT (spec item 7) IS A DOCUMENTED DISTRIBUTED MECHANISM, NOT A DROPPED ONE. It is carried by connector 3 `membrane_cytosol_boundary` as a SEMIPERMEABLE Kedem-Katchalsky boundary J = L_p(σΔΠ − ΔP) with an implicit extracellular reservoir, against the impermeable nuclear envelope, closing mass/no-flux/adjoint-work in one candidate (ac/engine/cytosol_connected.py:1-40). Constant Δπ = Π₀ is a ratified PI modelling decision, and Π₀'s provenance is declared (forces_manifest.py:376-377). No missing component.

ALL SIX FRAMEWORK DOUBLE-COUNTING TRAPS (CELL_MECHANICS_FRAMEWORK_2026-07-15.md:136-142) ARE STRUCTURALLY PREVENTED BY THE 13/32. (1) membrane and cortex are separate components joined only by ERM, so the two tensions cannot merge; (2) one pressure owner (cytosol Biot) delivers traction through the two boundaries, so turgor's Laplace partner cannot be re-added; (3) `nmii` is the only actuator — there is no active-stress component to stack on explicit heads; (4) fluid–solid dissipation has exactly one owner per pair (the six IMMERSED_TRANSFER connectors 2/14/15/16/19/23); (5) no fixed-FA boundary condition exists — 'FA | fixed world point | diagnostic rigid-substrate control only | non-production' (LOAD_PATH_PLAN.md:106) and world_boundary touches only ECM (measured deg=1); (6) one ECM component, 'no second ECM law' (COMPONENT_BUILD_MATRIX.md:30).

THE LOAD-TRANSFER FRAMING (3D/2D/1D/BC, framework:36-42) IS ENCODED IN `ComponentRole`: FLUID_VOLUME/CORE_BODY = 3D bulk, SURFACE_BODY = 2D shells, ACTIVE_LOAD_PATH/STRUCTURAL_RIG = 1D networks, ENVIRONMENT = boundary conditions, and the discrete-connector class is the ConnectorFamily enum (contracts.py:13-40). The only grouping difference is that ECM fibers are typed ENVIRONMENT rather than 1D-network, but its representation string is 'fiber/crosslink world' so no dimensional collapse occurs — cosmetic.

THE 12-ITEM COMPARTMENT ROADMAP MAPS ONTO THE 13 WITH NOTHING LOST. Roadmap items 1-10 map to components 1:1 (fluid→`cytosol`); item 11 'ECM + adhesion clutch + FA' correctly SPLITS into `ecm` + `focal_adhesion` (two different state owners: a fiber world vs a stochastic clutch graph); item 12 'Crosslinkers' becomes connectors + internal KMC; the 13th, `world_boundary`, is a considered addition, not drift — it is the framework's own boundary-condition class (framework:42) given an explicit owner so the far-field reaction is ledgered instead of implied. (COMPARTMENT_COMPLETION_ROADMAP_2026-07-22.md:32-45.)

THE CROSSLINKER RECLASSIFICATION (roadmap item 12 → connectors 29/30 + internal KMC) IS SOUND AND LOSES NO LOAD PATH BY ITSELF. It is literally the PI taxonomy: 'Discrete connectors | motors, crosslinkers, integrin, cadherin' (framework:41). Crosslinkers are not state-owning bodies; they are two-endpoint joints, and the contract forces every one of them to be bidirectional + adjoint + accepted-step-committed (contracts.py:96-119). Intra-component crosslinks (cortical α-actinin/filamin, fascin bundling, IF internal, ECM internal) stay component-internal by the same rule that both endpoints belong to one owner (INTERMEDIATE_FILAMENT_PLAN.md:93-94). The only crosslinker load paths actually missing are the plectin ones in gap #2 — a specific edge omission, not a consequence of the reclassification.

THE UNIFIED ACTIN CATEGORY IS FULLY HOUSED. The PI 2026-06-04 category 'cortex, lamellipodium, filopodium, stress-fibers, microvilli and traction apparatus' (FF_STAGE6L_UNIFIED_ARCHITECTURE_2026-06-30.md:15-18) maps to `cortex`/`lamellipodium`/`filopodium`/`sf_arc` + membrane-internal reservoir + `sf_arc`&`focal_adhesion`; the split into four disjoint components is the documented PI 2026-07-22 supersession, not drift, and the perinuclear actin cap is `sf_arc` + `actin_cap_linc`.

MYOSIN PORT TOPOLOGY IS CORRECT AND COMPLETE. `nmii` is a separate head-resolved actuator component with MOTOR ports on exactly the four actin components (25-28) and none on MT/IF/ECM/nucleus — NMII acts only on actin, and every port is kinetic with generation_required + remap_on_accept so head binding cannot survive a rejected step or a stale material coordinate (contracts.py:398-427).

MEMBRANE-CORTEX DETACHABILITY IS PRESERVED, so blebbing is expressible: ERM is a kinetic connector with an ezrin chemistry card rather than a welded boundary condition (contracts.py:253-257), exactly as the spec demands ('Interface = ERM membrane–cortex adhesion (NOT a fixed BC, or blebs/tethers can't form)', framework:76).

FRONT-TO-REAR GLOBAL LOAD PATHS EXIST TWICE OVER: the membrane is one component with in-plane tension (a single global surface load path) and the cytosol is one Biot/Darcy field touching 8 of 12 intracellular components (measured deg=8), so hydraulic and surface-tension coupling between the leading edge and the rear do not need any additional connector.

THE CHEMICAL_FLUX 32→36 REWIRING IS NOT A MECHANICAL GAP. The G-actin monomer path is already carried mechanically by the IMMERSED_TRANSFER connectors whose endpoint roles name the 'G-actin transport stencil' (contracts.py:358-363, 385-390); the pending 4 CHEMICAL_FLUX edges (monomer_flux.py:1-30) split a conserved scalar exchange out of them for A_total bookkeeping. It is a mass-ledger refinement awaiting PI sign-off, not a missing load path.

HEADLINE. The 13/32 graph is a faithful superset of the project's own specs for a single cell — 10 compartments and 12 roadmap items all land, world_boundary is a considered addition (the framework's BC class given an owner), and the crosslinker→connector reclassification is the PI taxonomy verbatim. Nothing in the graph is drift. The gaps are all ONE class: **the graph has almost no CONTACT/exclusion topology inside the cell.** CONTACT appears 3 times, all on the outer surface (lamellipodium/filopodium↔membrane, membrane↔ECM). Every interior pair is coupled by tension-carrying bonds only — LINC, plectin, spectraplakin, crosslink seams, motor ports — so components can PULL each other but cannot PUSH each other or refuse to interpenetrate. That is the exact opposite of the incumbent `ac/cell`, whose single label-blind all-fiber WCA (forces_manifest.py:260-262) covered cross-structure exclusion for free precisely because everything shared one array. The PI 2026-07-22 disjoint-population decision was right, but it silently dropped that coverage, and no roadmap rung (R0-R8, ROLLING_ROADMAP.md:195-300) restores it.

ANSWERS TO THE THREE LENS-3 QUESTIONS. (1) Only ONE spec entry has neither a component nor a documented component-internal home: compartment 9, the cell–cell junction (gap #4) — and it has a documented deferral to Multicell Part II (SINGLE_CELL_BUILDUP_PLAN:176), so it is scoping, not drift. Compartment 7 (volume/osmotic) has no component but IS a documented distributed mechanism (semipermeable membrane boundary + Π₀). Two spec sentences describe load paths the graph then narrowed without saying so: 'IF … tension net between nucleus and membrane' (framework:92-94, and SINGLE_CELL_BUILDUP_PLAN:93) became IF↔nucleus + IF↔SF only (gap #2); 'nucleus … largest steric bottleneck' (framework:110) has no contact edge (gap #1). (2) Nothing in the 13 is absent from the specs. world_boundary = framework:42 BC class; `nmii` = spec item 4; `focal_adhesion` split from ECM = spec item 8 vs 10. (3) Crosslinkers-as-connectors is sound and loses nothing structurally; the losses are specific plectin edges, reported separately.

WATCH ITEMS (deliberately NOT reported as gaps). (a) No connector transfers filament OWNERSHIP between the four actin components; the documented lamellipodium→transverse-arc conversion (Burnette-type) must therefore route through the G-actin pool rather than by relabelling filaments. Biologically defensible, but it means arc genesis is a nucleation event, not a conversion — worth an explicit note in the SF plan. (b) Active membrane-area GENERATION (exocytic addition) is distinct from unfolding the Raucher-Sheetz reservoir and is the mechanism `dcm/` identified as required for spreading; it lives inside `membrane` as a source term, so it is not an architecture gap, but the 13/32 has no A/A₀ observable at all (TRAJECTORY_HOW_WE_GOT_TO_AC_2026-07-25.md:217). (c) The 2026-07-07 compartment spec (COMPARTMENT_BUILD_PLAN_2026-07-07.md:148) additionally names glycocalyx, spectrin skeleton, septins, nucleolar LLPS and Piezo; all five are legitimately internal groupings (glycocalyx = a brush term in `membrane_ecm_contact`'s law, spectrin/septins = membrane/cortex internal, LLPS = nucleus internal, Piezo = a sensor, not a load path) — I checked each and none is a missing load path. (d) Lobopodial migration (nuclear pistoning, ACTIN_ARCHITECTURE_NOTES.md:386-401) needs the same nucleus↔cortex seal as gap #1 plus a cytosol domain that can split front/rear; it is out of the 2D MCF7 target but is the second consumer of that fix.

RECOMMENDED SEQUENCING IF THE PI WANTS ONE CHANGE. Add the CONTACT-family connector class first and instantiate `nucleus_cortex_contact` + `nucleus_membrane_contact` (gap #1): it is the only gap rated BLOCKS_DEFORMATION_COUPLING that is also on the critical path for an already-recorded failure mode (the S3 'nucleus pokes through the cortex' artifact), it reuses `membrane_ecm_contact`'s proven contract shape, and it needs no new sourced magnitude beyond a declared numerical exclusion stiffness. `if_cortex_plectin` (gap #2) is second and cheapest — it restores an edge whose kernel and passing coupling gate already exist in ac/solid/intermediate_filament.py.

gaps.structure: Cross-component tangent (the connector's off-diagonal stiffness block, ∂f_A/∂x_B). Nothing in the connector contract obliges a connector to deliver an operator action — only a force.
gaps.connects: Every connected component pair. Canonically membrane↔cortex through membrane_erm_cortex (k_erm = 4.6e3 pN/µm vs a membrane node's own γ_mem = 10 pN/µm — a 460× contrast), and nucleus↔sf_arc through actin_cap_linc.
gaps.why_architecture_cannot_express_it: ConnectorContract has 16 fields (name, family, component_a/b, kinetics, commit_on_accept, scope, endpoint_role_a/b, chemistry_card, mechanical_group, bidirectional, adjoint_transfer_required, generation_required, remap_on_accept, blocks_sleep_refine) — contracts.py:76-94. NOT ONE of them declares a tangent/Jacobian/operator action. CellActor._MECHANICS_HOOKS (actor.py:16-27) is ten names, all force accumulators (accumulate, accumulate_actor, accumulate_boundary, accumulate_candidate, accumulate_internal, accumulate_motor, accumulate_pair, accumulate_rig, accumulate_transfer, solve_candidate); assert_fully_bound (actor.py:128-129) admits a connector that exposes ANY ONE of them and never asks for a tangent. ComponentContract.solver is a per-component free-text string (contracts.py:58; the 11 distinct values are 'surface solve', 'graph mechanics', 'field solve', 'joint KMC', …) — there is no declaration of a global coupled system. world.py:5 states the design position explicitly: 'preserving one physical clock across independently solved components'. The architecture SoT asks COMPONENTS for 'tangent/operator action' (CELL_ENGINE_ARCHITECTURE.md:107) but its connector spec (§5, lines 100-121) lists only 'constitutive/force law' and 'equal-and-opposite reaction scatter'. A cross-component stiffness block therefore has no representation in the graph and can only be built by hand-writing a per-slice concatenated scratch outside it — which is exactly what ac/engine/sf_implicit.py:85-90 does for the single sf_arc+nmii pair ('allocates its OWN concatenated scratch [SF nodes | NMII particles] and gathers/scatters into it'). That pattern is O(n_pairs) hand-written combinations, not a graph capability.
gaps.observable_that_would_be_wrong: Exactly the already-measured failure, repeated. Force-only coupling with per-component solves is block-Jacobi with a one-pass lag: at the membrane→ERM→cortex interface the coupling stiffness is 460× the membrane's own diagonal and ~1/100 of the cortex crosslink diagonal (k_xl = 4.6e5 pN/µm, ff/hand_kmc.py:132), so a single lagged pass transmits essentially zero displacement — the project's own note gives the iteration's spectral radius as k_erm/√(D_mem·D_cortex) and says the membrane otherwise OVER-STEPS at turgor/(a+γ_area) (implicit_mechanics.py:1508-1512). Apply a point load to the cortex and the membrane, nucleus and MT respond by ~0 nm in one accepted step: 'cortex shell 39.8 nm | MT aster + MTOC 0.0 nm FROZEN — bit-identical rest vs load | nucleus 0.0 nm' (INTERNAL_DISPLACEMENT_DIAGNOSIS_2026-07-16.md:13-15).

gaps.proposed_fix: Add a tangent obligation to the connector contract, not to a slice: (a) a `tangent_required: bool` / `tangent_symmetry` field on ConnectorContract; (b) an `apply_tangent(vector_a, vector_b, out_a, out_b)` hook added to a new _TANGENT_HOOKS tuple in actor.py that assert_fully_bound REQUIRES of every non-kinetic-only connector; (c) a graph-level matrix-free operator that walks architecture.connectors and calls each connector's apply_tangent, so the coupled A·v is assembled FROM the graph instead of from a hand-written concatenation. gaps.structure: The coupled-candidate convergence criterion of one accepted physical step — CELL_ENGINE_ARCHITECTURE.md §6.3/§6.4 ('solve the coupled … mechanics to the registered convergence and conservation criteria' … 'refresh geometry, field transfers, and connector forces until the coupled candidate is consistent').
gaps.connects: All 13 components at once — it is the contract that makes the accepted step ONE mechanical system rather than 13 independent ones.
gaps.why_architecture_cannot_express_it: CellTransaction.step takes `solve: Callable[[], None]` (transaction.py:99-100) — no arguments, no return value, no residual channel, no iteration count — and calls it EXACTLY ONCE (transaction.py:129). There is no §6.4 'refresh until consistent' loop anywhere, and the transaction has no way to learn whether the coupled candidate converged, hence no way to reject on non-convergence. The only registered acceptance criterion in the graph is GlobalCellLedger.assemble_balance: |Σ far-field ECM reaction + Σ cell→ECM traction|² against a caller tolerance (ledger.py:126-146, 329-357) — a SINGLE 3-vector resultant across ONE cut, which is satisfied identically by any equal-and-opposite pair regardless of the per-DOF residual. A cortex in gross internal disequilibrium passes it. CellCandidatePipeline.run_candidate is one pass and defers iteration to 'the enclosing nonlinear/world solver' (dispatch.py:322-329) — which does not exist: ComposedNativeCell.solve_candidate (composed_native.py:347-360) zeroes each owner's force array, runs run_candidate() once, computes motor loads, and NEVER integrates a position. The composed native accepted step has no solver and no integrator. (VERIFIED, not inferred: the whole-project audit's claim is correct.)
gaps.observable_that_would_be_wrong: A load applied anywhere propagates zero distance in one accepted step, and no compartment can deform another, because nothing moves at all. The only driver of the composed cell (scripts/ac_gate_b_composed_native.py) demonstrates this: it perturbs the SF and ECM positions from the HOST with numpy and wp.copy (lines 223-229), then calls step_once once (line 234) and reads back forces (lines 238-245). Its 'VERDICT PASS' (line 285) certifies that force appeared, not that geometry responded. Same in the interior-column slice: the native driver's `solve` is the INCUMBENT `make_inner_solve(cell, …, inner_solver='explicit')` (scripts/ac_gate_b_interior_column_native.py:283-288), so InteriorColumnSlice.accumulate (interior_column_slice.py:544-565) — which is where all three fluid connectors' adjoint force pairs live — is never invoked in that run at all. Because the transaction cannot reject on non-convergence, every quantitative number a composed step produces is a relaxation transient, which is precisely the already-recorded failure mode: 'the free-node residual sat at ~15% of the reported tension, and a 10x longer relax moved T_max by 3.4x at an identical bound population' (sf_implicit.py:5-8).

gaps.structure: Plectin cytolinker cross-bridges of the IF↔F-actin(cortex) and IF↔microtubule kinds — the two edges that make actin/MT/IF ONE tri-network instead of three.
gaps.connects: intermediate_filament ↔ cortex, and intermediate_filament ↔ microtubule.
gaps.why_architecture_cannot_express_it: `intermediate_filament` has exactly three edges in the 32 — if_nucleus_linc, if_sf_plectin, if_cytosol_transfer (contracts.py:310-322,339-343); computed adjacency is {cytosol, nucleus, sf_arc}. `microtubule` has four — mt_nucleus_linc, mt_cortex_capture, mt_sf_spectraplakin, mt_cytosol_transfer — adjacency {cortex, cytosol, nucleus, sf_arc}, no IF partner. Because cortex and sf_arc are DISJOINT filament populations by PI decision (2026-07-22), if_sf_plectin CANNOT reach a cortex filament: architecture.force_path('intermediate_filament','cortex') returns ('intermediate_filament','cytosol','cortex') and force_path('intermediate_filament','microtubule') returns ('intermediate_filament','cytosol','microtubule'). Both shortest routes go through the CYTOSOL — a Biot/Darcy pore-pressure + drag field, which transmits no deviatoric (shear) load at equilibrium and cannot carry a cross-bridge tension. Adding either edge requires a new ConnectorContract; there is no way to route it. This was a deliberate deletion, recorded: 'The cortex anchor is not the registered composition. The common engine graph declares if_nucleus_linc and if_sf_plectin; the legacy wrapper hard-wires a nearest-cortex spring instead of an SF/arc plectin endpoint' (INTERMEDIATE_FILAMENT_PLAN.md:53-55).
gaps.observable_that_would_be_wrong: The IF cage becomes a cage hanging off the nucleus and a sparse SF population, with no shear connection to the shell that actually deforms. Cortical strain then cannot reach the nucleus by any solid route — which reproduces the native measurement the graph was built to fix: cortex 39.8 nm, MT aster 0.0 nm, nucleus 0.0 nm, nucleus flattening 0.0% under a 10% plate strain (INTERNAL_DISPLACEMENT_DIAGNOSIS_2026-07-16.md:13-17). That document's own prescribed fix B is the missing edge verbatim: 'IF cage … linking nucleus surface ↔ cortex. Transmits cortex DEFORMATION to the nucleus' (:47-49). Downstream: MT compression struts cannot be pre-loaded against the IF/actin tension net, so the tensegrity load-sharing that stops a LOCAL cortical failure from becoming a GLOBAL one has no representation — the project states this consequence itself: 'Without them the framework-3c load-distribution / prevent-local->global-failure role cannot emerge' (KB_UPLOAD_MANIFEST_2026-07-15.md:230).

gaps.structure: The nucleus's coupling to the cell's outer shell: (a) a solid nucleus↔cortex tether (nesprin/LINC to cortical F-actin, plus the perinuclear vimentin cage), and (b) volumetric steric non-penetration contact between the nuclear envelope and the cortex/plasma membrane.
gaps.connects: nucleus ↔ cortex, and nucleus ↔ membrane.
gaps.why_architecture_cannot_express_it: `nucleus` has exactly four edges — nucleus_cytosol_boundary, actin_cap_linc (sf_arc), mt_nucleus_linc, if_nucleus_linc (contracts.py:268-272,290-316); computed adjacency {cytosol, intermediate_filament, microtubule, sf_arc}. There is NO cortex edge and NO membrane edge: force_path('cortex','nucleus') = ('cortex','cytosol','nucleus') and force_path('nucleus','membrane') = ('nucleus','cytosol','membrane') — both through the pore-fluid field only. And all three CONTACT-family connectors in the 32 are lamellipodium_membrane_contact, filopodium_membrane_tip, membrane_ecm_contact (contracts.py:344-350,371-377,445-450); none involves the nucleus, so non-penetration between the envelope and the shell is not declarable. nucleus_cytosol_boundary is a FLUID_BOUNDARY with kinetics=False: a Darcy/Biot pore fluid DRAINS, so pressure cannot enforce a geometric constraint. The already-working incumbent link is the one the graph deletes: the incumbent's LINC tether is nucleus node ↔ **cortex anchor** (compartments.py:289-290 'linc_a_d … cortex anchor'), it sits in the coupled implicit operator (implicit_mechanics.py:1770-1773) and is the ONLY solid cortex→nucleus path that has ever worked — and it has no home among the 32, which offer only sf_arc↔nucleus. Steric exclusion is likewise structurally off, not merely unimplemented: the WCA mask marks every non-actin node dormant, 'active<0 → EV skips myosin/nucleus/membrane' (assemble.py:815-819).
gaps.observable_that_would_be_wrong: In a spread adherent MCF7 the cell height over the nucleus (~4-6 µm) is less than the unflattened nuclear diameter (~10 µm), so the flattened nuclear shape is produced by the dorsal cortex/membrane pressing on the envelope. With no contact and no cortex tether the nucleus does not flatten — measured exactly: 'nucleus flattening under the plate: 0.0 % (z-half 5.106 → 5.106 µm)' (INTERNAL_DISPLACEMENT_DIAGNOSIS_2026-07-16.md:17). Worse, at any larger deformation the envelope passes THROUGH the cortex and membrane, which is geometric nonsense; and the nucleus, which is the rate-limiting obstacle for migration through ECM pores, stops limiting anything. Note the actin cap (actin_cap_linc) cannot substitute: a LINC tether pulls, it cannot push, so compressive confinement is unrepresentable through it.

(1) `nucleus_cortex_linc` — ConnectorFamily.LINC, nucleus ↔ cortex, kinetic + commit_on_accept, generation_required/remap_on_accept/blocks_sleep_refine like the other three LINCs; this simply gives the incumbent's already-working cortex-anchored LINC tether (compartments.py:290) a legal home instead of retiring it during the Card-5 strangler. gaps.structure: The adhesion plaque's anchors other than the stress fiber: focal_adhesion ↔ plasma membrane (integrin is a transmembrane protein; the adhesion is what holds the bilayer against the ECM) and focal_adhesion ↔ cortex (talin/vinculin bind basal cortical F-actin, not only SF bundles).
gaps.connects: focal_adhesion ↔ membrane, and focal_adhesion ↔ cortex.
gaps.why_architecture_cannot_express_it: `focal_adhesion` has exactly four edges — fa_actin_anchor (sf_arc), integrin_collagen_clutch (ecm), lamellipodium_nascent_fa, filopodium_nascent_fa; computed adjacency {ecm, filopodium, lamellipodium, sf_arc}. No membrane, no cortex. Consequently the graph's shortest cortex→substrate route is force_path('cortex','ecm') = ('cortex','membrane','ecm') — i.e. through the ERM tether and then `membrane_ecm_contact`, which is declared kinetics=False, commit_on_accept=False (contracts.py:445-450): a NON-ADHESIVE steric contact. The cortex therefore has no adhesive path to the ECM at all; every adhesive route must pass through sf_arc/lamellipodium/filopodium. This is not routable around, for two structural reasons: focal_adhesion is declared owns_geometry=False (contracts.py:218-221) so it has no material point that a third partner could attach to, and ConnectorContract is strictly binary (component_a, component_b — contracts.py:78-79), so a real multi-body plaque (collagen + integrin-in-bilayer + one or more actin populations) cannot be declared as one junction. Each extra partner needs its own new ConnectorContract into a geometry-less joint.
gaps.observable_that_would_be_wrong: Two things. (i) The basal plasma membrane is held down by nothing adhesive: under the resting turgor (Π₀ ≈ 40 Pa) it would balloon away from the substrate between adhesions and the cell would sit on the ECM like a pressurised bag touching through a repulsive contact, instead of the ~30-50 nm membrane-substrate apposition at adhesions that FA nanoscale architecture measurements show. Correspondingly, traction never loads the bilayer, so the membrane-tension ↔ adhesion ↔ protrusion feedback that couples a crawling cell's front to its rear has no mechanical representation. (ii) Cortical actomyosin tension produces no substrate traction anywhere except at SF ends and protrusions — so in an epithelial cell with poorly developed stress fibers the whole-cell traction map is empty over the cell body, and pulling on the substrate does not deform the cortex.
