gaps.proposed_fix: Either (a) add two ConnectorContracts — `fa_membrane_anchor` (ConnectorFamily.ACTIN_ANCHOR or a new TRANSMEMBRANE family; focal_adhesion ↔ membrane, kinetic, endpoint roles 'FA integrin-ectodomain state' / 'membrane material point') and `fa_cortex_anchor` (focal_adhesion ↔ cortex, ConnectorFamily.ACTIN_ANCHOR, endpoint role 'basal cortical actin material point'), both joined to the existing alpha2beta1_collagen_series mechanical_group so CellActor's group-identity guard (actor.py:55-62) keeps the plaque ONE runtime object and not springs in series; or (b) give focal_adhesion owns_geometry=True (a plaque material point) so the plaque becomes a hub and each partner is an ordinary binary edge to it — the cleaner fix, and the only one that scales to a real multi-body junction.

gaps.structure: Immersed viscous/porous drag on the NMII minifilament population (nmii ↔ cytosol IMMERSED_TRANSFER).
gaps.connects: nmii ↔ cytosol.
gaps.why_architecture_cannot_express_it: There are exactly six IMMERSED_TRANSFER connectors — surface_porous_transfer (cortex), sf_cytosol_transfer, mt_cytosol_transfer, if_cytosol_transfer, lamellipodium_cytosol_transfer, filopodium_cytosol_transfer — plus two FLUID_BOUNDARY edges for membrane and nucleus. `nmii` is declared owns_geometry=True, dynamically_evolving=True (contracts.py:238-242) yet its adjacency is {cortex, filopodium, lamellipodium, sf_arc}: it is the ONLY geometry-owning, dynamically-evolving component in the graph with no coupling to the cytosol at all. force_path('nmii','cytosol') = ('nmii','cortex','cytosol') — i.e. a minifilament can only feel the fluid through actin it happens to be BOUND to, and an UNBOUND minifilament feels nothing. Adding the edge requires a new ConnectorContract.
gaps.observable_that_would_be_wrong: An unbound minifilament is a force-free rigid body with zero drag: its motion is set by whatever numerical mobility the solver supplies rather than by physics, and the mechanical operator is singular on its 6 rigid-body modes. The engine already relies on a numerical device to hide this: 'a = regularization[0] … is what makes the operator non-singular for the parts of this slice that are genuinely unanchored … every unbound minifilament is a free rigid body' (sf_implicit.py:66-72). Physically wrong consequences: the spatial distribution of the free NMII pool, its diffusive re-binding statistics, and therefore the emergent bound fraction (the quantity the GATE-B cortex run reports rising 0 → 84%) all depend on an unphysical mobility instead of the sourced cytosol viscosity/permeability.

The turgor/osmotic load path is complete and expressible: cytosol pressure → membrane (membrane_cytosol_boundary), → cortex (surface_porous_transfer), → nuclear envelope (nucleus_cytosol_boundary), with the membrane as the semipermeable osmotic envelope. result.notes:
DIRECT ANSWERS TO (1)-(4).

(1) ONE accepted step propagation, and what prevents a repeat of the 39.8 nm / 0.0 nm failure.
Through the ENGINE GRAPH: nothing propagates, because the composed accepted step has no solver and no integrator (composed_native.py:347-360; transaction.py:129 calls solve() once). Through the INCUMBENT: yes for four compartments and only four. cell.pos_d is ONE merged vector [actin(cortex) | myosin | nucleus | membrane] (assemble.py:754-810, n_total at :810) solved by one PCG over all n_total DOFs (implicit_mechanics.py:1481) whose operator carries the ERM, LINC and crossbridge off-diagonal blocks (:1775, :1770, :1764). So cortex↔membrane↔nucleus↔nmii DO deform each other in one step.
What structurally prevents a repeat: for the NUCLEUS, genuinely fixed — the nucleus is now inside the coupled DOF vector with a cortex-anchored LINC tangent block. For MT and IF, NOTHING prevents a repeat: `_accumulate_all` (driver.py:140-168) contains no MT, no IF, no ECM, no sf_arc, no lamellipodium, no filopodium force at all, and those populations are not in cell.pos_d. Six of the thirteen components are outside every coupled solve that exists. Note the irony: the nucleus's working solid link is nucleus↔CORTEX LINC (compartments.py:290), an edge the declared 32-connector graph does NOT contain — so migrating the incumbent onto the graph as declared would REINTRODUCE the failure it fixed. That is Gap 4.

(2) Simultaneity: the graph permits staggered, and does not require simultaneous.
Nothing in the graph requires a coupled system. ComponentContract.solver is a per-component string (contracts.py:58); world.py:5 states the intent as 'one physical clock across independently solved components'; CELL_ENGINE_ARCHITECTURE.md:135 explicitly allows partitioned solvers. Staggering is NOT wrong per se — block Gauss-Seidel converges to the monolithic fixed point IF the outer coupling loop is iterated to convergence. What breaks is TRUNCATION, and the executable contract truncates at exactly one pass. Concretely wrong, with numbers from the repo: at the membrane–ERM–cortex interface the diagonals are γ_mem = 10 pN/µm (compartments.py:121), k_erm = 4.6e3 (compartments.py:123), k_xl = 4.6e5 (ff/hand_kmc.py:132) — a 1 : 460 : 46,000 ladder. A single force-lagged pass is exact only in the weak-coupling limit k_c → 0; here the coupling is the STIFFEST thing the membrane node sees, so the transmitted displacement is off by O(1) and the project's own note records both failure directions: without the tension-side ERM diagonal the membrane OVER-STEPS at turgor/(a+γ_area), with it the coupled Jacobi radius is k_erm/√(D_mem·D_cortex) (implicit_mechanics.py:1508-1512). Because the transaction never sees a residual, it cannot tell one converged sweep from one truncated sweep. That is Gap 2, and it is the fix: not 'go monolithic', but 'give the coupling loop a residual and a termination criterion'.

(3) Are connector Jacobians available to the solver? NO — forces only. Verified structurally, not inferred: ConnectorContract's 16 fields contain no tangent/stiffness/operator declaration (contracts.py:76-94, confirmed by dataclasses.fields at runtime); CellActor._MECHANICS_HOOKS is ten names, every one a force accumulator, and assert_fully_bound admits a connector exposing any ONE of them (actor.py:16-27, 128-129). The architecture SoT asks COMPONENTS for 'tangent/operator action' (CELL_ENGINE_ARCHITECTURE.md:107) but its connector spec lists only 'constitutive/force law' + 'equal-and-opposite reaction scatter' (§5, :100-121) — so the one object that OWNS the cross-component block is the one object never asked for it. Yes: force-only coupling + per-component solves is the block-diagonal failure in a new costume, and that is what exists today. The single counter-example is ac/engine/sf_implicit.py, which builds a real coupled tangent for sf_arc+nmii — by hand-allocating a concatenated scratch OUTSIDE the graph (:85-90). That does not generalise: it is one hand-written module per component pair.

(4) Force-real vs declared-only — my independent count is STRICTER than the audit's 9/4/19. Using the criterion 'the connector's own force kernel actually executes through the engine graph in a native run, scattering equal-and-opposite onto both endpoints', I get 4 / 4 / 24.
FORCE-REAL (4): nmii_cortex_motor (cortex_motor_slice.py CortexMotorConnector; native scripts/ac_gate_b_cortex_motor_native.py; split crossbridge +f on head, −(1−t)f/−t·f on the two cortex segment nodes); nmii_sf_motor (sf_motor_slice.py:326-333; native scripts/ac_gate_b_sf_motor_native.py, the only slice with an implicit coupled solve); membrane_erm_cortex (erm_cortex_connector.py:114 ErmCortexConnector, built erm_cortex_slice.py:266, native scripts/ac_gate_b_erm_cortex_native.py:307); dorsal_arc_crosslink (INTERNAL to sf_arc; sf_mechanics.py SFInternalArcJointConnector, built composed_native.py:266, native scripts/ac_gate_b_sf_arc_native.py).
ONE-SIDED or BYPASSED (4): surface_porous_transfer, membrane_cytosol_boundary, nucleus_cytosol_boundary — real runtimes ARE constructed on the CUDA lane (scripts/ac_gate_b_interior_column_native.py:257-266) but InteriorColumnSlice.accumulate, where all three adjoint force pairs live (interior_column_slice.py:544-565), is NEVER invoked, because the driver's solve is the incumbent make_inner_solve (:283-288) and the module's own docstring concedes 'in the native no-double-count driver the compartment mechanics are no-ops'. In the executed path the cortex traction comes from the incumbent one-way PressureCoupling (driver.py:167; two-way Biot FSI is default-off), so it is fluid→solid only. Plus ecm_far_field_anchor: real one-sided Dirichlet reaction kernels (ecm_world.py:395-435) but FarFieldDirichletBoundaryRuntime is constructed only in tests.
DECLARED-ONLY (24): fa_actin_anchor, integrin_collagen_clutch (LoadPathJointRuntime is a linear spring built only in tests; no clutch KMC and no alpha2beta1 hazard law), sf_cortex_transient, actin_cap_linc, mt_nucleus_linc, mt_cortex_capture, if_nucleus_linc, if_sf_plectin, mt_sf_spectraplakin, sf_cytosol_transfer, mt_cytosol_transfer, if_cytosol_transfer, all 8 protrusion edges (ProtrusionGraphConnector.accumulate_actor takes ONE endpoint view — protrusion.py:126-145 — and LamellipodiumBranchAngleMechanics / FilopodiumFascinBundleMechanics are never constructed outside tests), nmii_lamellipodium_motor, nmii_filopodium_motor, membrane_ecm_contact, and ecm_crosslink. 4+4+24 = 32.
So the deformation coupling that exists TODAY through the graph is: nmii↔cortex, nmii↔sf_arc, membrane↔cortex, and sf_arc-internal. Everything the PI asked for — the cortex crumpling as one object under a substrate load, and a lamellipodium remodelling the ECM and moving the cell forward — currently runs on ZERO force-real connectors between the cortex/membrane and the ECM.

ONE MORE FINDING WORTH THE PI'S ATTENTION, reported here rather than as an architectural gap because the connector IS declared: there is no collagen crosslink force kernel anywhere in the tree. ECM mechanics has only the per-segment axial stiffness and bending-alpha kernels (ecm_mechanics.py:188,207); ECMInternalCrosslink is a Protocol with docstring-only methods (ecm_world.py:157-181). A Mikado fiber network with no inter-fiber crosslink force has no shear modulus and cannot transmit traction between fibers, so 'the cell remodels the ECM' has no load path in the executed code even though `ecm_crosslink` is properly declared with kinetics + generation + remap. This is implementation status, not architecture — but it is on the critical path for the PI's second worked example.

CAVEAT ON EXTERNAL LOADS (below the reporting bar, flagged for completeness): world_boundary connects ONLY to ecm (adjacency {ecm}) and owns no geometry (contracts.py:246-250). There is therefore no way to apply an external mechanical load or a rigid confining boundary to the cell except through the ECM fiber network — no AFM cantilever, compression plate, micropipette, or channel wall endpoint. The 2026-07-16 diagnosis that produced the 39.8 nm / 0.0 nm measurement used exactly such a plate, and the project's own conclusion was 'rigid = the right answer, soft plate = a 200× artifact'. This is expressible approximately (pin the ECM z_lo face via FAR_FIELD_DIRICHLET, as scripts/ac_gate_b_composed_native.py:192 does) so I did not report it as a gap, but the standard 2D configuration all the MCF7 traction/spreading data come from — cell on a collagen-coated RIGID coverslip — cannot be represented at the correct substrate modulus by a Mikado network whose effective stiffness is 12 Pa - 14 kPa.

METHOD NOTE: read-only throughout; no file was edited and no git write command was run. All architecture adjacencies and force paths above were computed live from ffn_sim.ac.engine.contracts.reference_cell_architecture() (13 components / 32 connectors confirmed; family census: 6 immersed_transfer, 5 motor, 4 transient_actin, 3 actin_anchor, 3 linc, 3 contact, 2 fluid_boundary, 1 each erm/fa_clutch/plectin/spectraplakin/fiber_crosslink/environment_boundary).

gaps.structure: Ventral cortical clutch — the integrin/talin/vinculin linkage between a VENTRAL CORTEX F-actin filament and the ECM (a `cortex <-> focal_adhesion` ACTIN_ANCHOR edge, i.e. the cortical/lamellar arm of the motor-clutch: Chan & Odde, Science 2008;322:1687; Gardel et al., J Cell Biol 2008;183:999)
gaps.connects: cortex (the 70,686-filament shell that owns essentially all of the cell's contractile surface tension) <-> focal_adhesion -> ecm -> world_boundary. Today the cortex's only route to ground is 2 hops through `sf_cortex_transient`, which the plan declares OPTIONAL and finite-lifetime, into sf_arc.
gaps.why_architecture_cannot_express_it: reference_cell_architecture() gives cortex the neighbour set {cytosol, filopodium, lamellipodium, membrane, microtubule, nmii, sf_arc} - no focal_adhesion, no ecm (contracts.py:252-451, verified live by neighbors('cortex')). COMPONENT_BUILD_MATRIX.md:24 lists cortex's ports as "ERM<->membrane, drag<->cytosol, SF seam, MT capture, protrusion roots" - adhesion is absent by design. LOAD_PATH_PLAN.md:22-24 states "Cortex is not the default SF anchor"; :104 makes SF<->cortex "optional, dynamic"; :105 forbids any permanent cortex weld. Because populations are DISJOINT (population.py:1-31, every filament belongs to exactly ONE component), a ventral cortical filament sitting on an integrin cannot be relabelled sf_arc without being removed from the cortex, so the cortex itself is left with no tangential edge to the substrate. The only cortex-side route to the ECM is via membrane, and `membrane_ecm_contact` is non-kinetic pure steric (contracts.py:445-450) - normal load only, no grip. This is a REGRESSION: the project's only validated crawl gripped CORTEX nodes directly to collagen (scripts/ff_crawl_on_substrate.py:159 `basal = np.where(cortex_pos[:,2] < z_sub+contact_h)`, :187 `attach_clutches_to_ecm(cortex_pos[basal])`, two-sided kernel at ff/fa_ecm.py:26-50). The 32-connector graph cannot express its own predecessor's traction channel.
gaps.observable_that_would_be_wrong: (1) Substrate traction under the cell BODY is identically zero; the TFM map becomes point dipoles at SF ends and the leading edge only, whereas real spread epithelia show distributed sub-body traction. (2) ZERO-SUM FLAG: `nmii_cortex_motor` on a closed cortical shell is an isotropic surface tension - net force exactly zero, and with no tangential edge to FA/ECM its ONLY external effect is the Laplace pressure balance. Cortical contractility therefore contributes exactly 0 pN of substrate traction and 0 to locomotion no matter how large it gets. This is the architectural form of the recorded ff/ failure ("the radial grip vector-cancels laterally", MDA_MB_231_MIGRATION_ROOTCAUSE_2026-07-14.md:44-50). (3) Rear retraction, which is a cortical rather than an SF event, cannot deliver its released load forward. (4) Ablate SFs (blebbistatin/ROCK-i, or an early-spreading cell) and the model cell has zero substrate anchorage and detaches.

All three CONTACT-family connectors (lamellipodium_membrane_contact, filopodium_membrane_tip, membrane_ecm_contact) sit on the membrane's OUTER face. ac/nucleus/INTEGRATION.md:77-79 states the intended mechanism explicitly: "The nucleus envelope's steric interaction with cortex filaments is the I2b StericForce (one steric channel), NOT a second nucleus-specific contact kernel" - i.e. a SHARED global excluded-volume array, exactly the co-location the engine contract forbids (CELL_ENGINE_ARCHITECTURE.md:110 "Concatenating two components into one array is not a connection"). And that shared channel is switched off anyway: ac/cell/assemble.py:818-820 sets active=-1 for nucleus and membrane nodes with the comment "<0 dormant -> EV skips myosin/nucleus/membrane", and steric_warp.py:97-112 is filament-filament only, keyed by fiber_id. ac/nucleus/INTEGRATION.md:73-76 then makes it a declared invariant: "The nucleus<->cytoskeleton load path is EITHER the LINC tether ... there is no second radial-strut nucleus anchor." The nucleus can be pulled and pressurised; it can never be squeezed.

gaps.structure: Lateral elastic reinforcement of the microtubule lattice by the surrounding intermediate-filament / cytoplasmic network - an `intermediate_filament <-> microtubule` plectin-sidearm edge (Svitkina et al., J Cell Biol 1996;135:991; Gan et al., Cell Syst 2016;3:252). The mechanics is Brangwynne et al., J Cell Biol 2006;173:733, "Microtubules can bear enhanced compressive loads in living cells because of lateral reinforcement."
gaps.connects: microtubule lattice, along its length rather than only at its plus end <-> intermediate_filament network. Today MT's neighbour set is {cortex, cytosol, nucleus, sf_arc}: the cortex and nucleus edges are surface/end couplings and the cytosol edge is IMMERSED_TRANSFER (viscous porous drag, not elastic).
gaps.why_architecture_cannot_express_it: There is no IF<->MT connector at all (verified: neighbors('microtubule') = cortex, cytosol, nucleus, sf_arc). The only distributed lateral elastic partner declared for an interior MT is mt_sf_spectraplakin, which exists only where a stress fiber runs alongside. The cytosol component solves pressure / relative flux / concentration, not a solid displacement field (CELL_ENGINE_ARCHITECTURE.md:62), so it supplies drag and pressure work, never elastic support. This is the ONE piece of the tensegrity load path that the connector architecture cannot express: the topological edges MT<->cortex, MT<->sf_arc, MT<->nucleus and the internal MTOC hub all exist, so MT is NOT architecturally a passenger any more (the old ff/ block-diagonal-K defect, CYTOSKELETON_CYTOSOL_REAUDIT_2026-07-16.md:43, is now structurally forbidden) - but the compression it can actually carry collapses to the free-rod value.
gaps.observable_that_would_be_wrong: MT critical compressive load and buckling wavelength. Unreinforced pinned-pinned Euler load for EI = 2.2e-23 N*m^2 (Gittes et al. 1993) at L = 10 um is F_c = pi^2*EI/L^2 = 2.2 pN. Brangwynne 2006 measured in-cell MTs buckling at short (~few um) wavelengths, i.e. bearing roughly two orders of magnitude more compression because of the surrounding elastic network. Without this edge the model MT buckles at ~2 pN, carries ~0 compression against a cortex loaded at tens-to-hundreds of pN, and the actin-tension / MT-compression balance the PI wants (tensegrity, nuclear positioning, MT-dependent shape stability) reverts numerically to the "MT = inert passenger" result the project already recorded.

Every edge exists; 5 and 6 correctly resolve to ONE composite series clutch with a mandatory double-count guard (LOAD_PATH_PLAN.md:199-215); 31 is non-kinetic so ground is always present. The path is a genuine dipole (net force zero, as inertialess mechanics requires) and produces motion when combined with adhesion asymmetry, which is expressible as component state.

(b) PROTRUSION REACTION GROUNDS. lamellipodium polymerisation -[17 lamellipodium_membrane_contact]-> membrane (forward thrust); the equal-and-opposite reaction leaves the network by two routes: -[18 lamellipodium_cortex_seam]-> cortex (internal Newton pair, net zero on the cell, correct) and -[20 lamellipodium_nascent_fa]-> focal_adhesion -[6]-> ecm -[31]-> world_boundary. The second route is grounded and it exists. The ff/ failure mode (the front slip reaction delivered to a MOVABLE collagen node that then drags the cell back, MDA_MB_231_MIGRATION_ROOTCAUSE_2026-07-14.md:51-54) is a coherence/magnitude problem INSIDE this graph, not a missing edge: connector 31 grounds the ECM elastically, and both prescribed fixes (that doc, section 5 - rear-retraction traction; uncancelled front anchorage) are expressible as state on connectors 25/26, 6 and 31. On a 3D matrix the front thrust additionally has [32 membrane_ecm_contact].

(c) NUCLEUS LOADING CLOSES IN TENSION. ecm -[6]-> focal_adhesion -[5]-> sf_arc -[8 actin_cap_linc]-> nucleus -> lamina/chromatin (component-internal, forces_manifest.py:416-434). Parallel routes: [9 mt_nucleus_linc], [11 if_nucleus_linc], and the hydrostatic route membrane -[3]-> cytosol -[4]-> nucleus. Substrate strain therefore reaches the lamina. Only the compression/confinement half is missing (gap 2).

(d) TURGOR CLOSES. cytosol -[3 membrane_cytosol_boundary]-> membrane and cytosol -[2 surface_porous_transfer]-> cortex (drag + pressure work, CELL_ENGINE_ARCHITECTURE.md:30); the reaction is membrane areal tension plus cortical tension, net force exactly zero (correct Young-Laplace); the nucleus is loaded by the same pressure via [4]. No mechanical edge is missing here; transfer QUALITY is limited by the tether-only ERM (gap 3) and by the constant-d_pi choice (gap 7).

(e) TENSEGRITY IS ARCHITECTURALLY EXPRESSIBLE - MT IS NO LONGER A PASSENGER BY CONSTRUCTION. The MT component owns a live MTOC hub that accumulates every arm's Newton-3rd minus-end reaction (microtubule_rig.py:555-566, 636-662; non-alias guard at :345), and its connector protocol explicitly admits an "MT material/MTOC endpoint" (:137), so the aster's summed reaction can be delivered through [9 mt_nucleus_linc] to the nucleus, while load enters laterally through [13 mt_sf_spectraplakin] and [10 mt_cortex_capture] (whose endpoint role admits lattice motor sites, not only plus ends). The old block-diagonal-K failure came from merged arrays and is structurally forbidden now. Only the lateral-reinforcement magnitude collapses (gap 5).

(f) IF IS NOT A DEAD END. intermediate_filament -[12 if_sf_plectin]-> sf_arc -[5]-> focal_adhesion -[6]-> ecm -[31]-> world_boundary, plus [11 if_nucleus_linc] to the nucleus. IF tension terminates on ground, not in a floating internal pair. The gap is the missing PERIPHERAL anchor (gap 4), not an unterminated path.

(g) REAR RETRACTION CLOSES. Release is kinetic and accepted-step-gated on [6 integrin_collagen_clutch] and [5 fa_actin_anchor] (kinetics=True, commit_on_accept=True; 6 additionally generation_required + remap_on_accept + blocks_sleep_refine). The released load is carried forward by nmii -[25/26]-> sf_arc/cortex tension -[5]-> front FA -[6]-> ecm. Membrane area recovery is the component-internal Raucher-Sheetz reservoir. Caveat: because real rear retraction is cortical rather than SF-borne, transmission quality depends on gap 1.

(h) ECM PLASTIC MEMORY CLOSES. The ECM component owns damage/remodelling/refinement/topology state and refuses to build without it (ecm_world.py:139-152: "production ECM requires remodelling and damage state"); [30 ecm_crosslink] is kinetic with generation_required + remap_on_accept; all of it commits atomically only on an accepted step (ecm_world.py:706-744, 1027). The permanently altered fibre configuration re-enters the cell as the boundary condition of the next step through [6] and [32]. Only mass-changing remodelling is missing (gap 6).
Chromatin + lamin-A/C + lamin-B are correctly component-internal to nucleus (forces_manifest.py:416-434; contracts.py:210-214).

Microvilli / membrane folds as the membrane's area reservoir, and the crosslinker families via [29 dorsal_arc_crosslink] / [30 ecm_crosslink] plus component-internal crosslink KMC, are correctly internal - not missing components.

G-actin monomer field and poroelastic pore fluid are correctly internal to cytosol, with the conserved-pool draw/return convention specified (WHOLE_CELL_COMMON_CONTRACTS_SPEC_2026-07-23.md section 4) and implemented (ac/engine/monomer_flux.py).

Force continuity across the moving boundary is [18 lamellipodium_cortex_seam]; identity is handled by the free-list discipline (population.py:11-31 - nucleation pops a dormant slot, depolymerisation returns one), so rear-lamellipodial disassembly plus cortical nucleation is expressible without violating the disjoint unique-ID invariant, and it matches the observed lamellipodium/lamella kinetic boundary rather than requiring cross-component ownership transfer.

The FA composite series joint (fa_actin_anchor + integrin_collagen_clutch resolving to one clutch with two ports) and the explicitly forbidden edges (arc -> FA; permanent SF -> cortex weld) are correctly specified and pre-empt the classic double-stiffness error (LOAD_PATH_PLAN.md:95-109, 199-215).

Cell-cell junctions (adherens/desmosome/cadherin) are correctly absent for the audited scene - a SINGLE adherent cell has none. They become a required component/connector pair only when the EMT / epithelial-cluster target arrives, and cadherin has already been ratified as a catch-bond mechanism to add then.
result.notes:
SCOPE AND BAR. Judged against the PI's stated priority (mechanical connectedness, not magnitudes) and the strict bar: a load path a real adherent crawling epithelial cell HAS that this graph cannot express even in principle. I dropped several plausible candidates for failing that bar: MTOC/centrosome (component-internal live hub whose connector protocol admits MTOC endpoints); lamellipodium-to-cortex population transfer (expressible via the free-list); hemidesmosome / alpha6beta4-keratin (laminin ligand, does not form on collagen-I, out of scope for MCF7-on-collagen); cortex-internal crosslink KMC and membrane trafficking (declared internal); external hydrodynamic drag (negligible at Re ~1e-10). All 32 edges were cross-checked by executing reference_cell_architecture() live in the ffn_sim env (13 components / 32 connectors confirmed; adjacency sets printed and quoted in the evidence fields). No files were modified.

THE MOST VALUABLE FINDING - A PATH THAT EXISTS BUT SUMS TO ZERO. nmii_cortex_motor is the single best-evidenced force-real connector in the engine (85% head binding, gamma 0 -> 3.72 emergent at 70,686 filaments), and in this graph its work is 100% internally cancelled. Myosin contracting a closed cortical shell is an isotropic surface tension: net force exactly zero, and because the cortex has NO tangential edge to focal_adhesion or ecm, that tension cannot appear in the substrate traction at all - the Laplace/pressure balance is its only external effect. So the project's strongest connector contributes exactly 0 pN of locomotory traction, and the sub-body traction field of an adherent epithelial cell is identically zero. This is the architectural restatement of the ff/ crawl root cause ("the radial grip vector-cancels laterally ... F_net = one quarter to one clutch", MDA_MB_231_MIGRATION_ROOTCAUSE_2026-07-14.md:44-72) - and note the fix specified there was never applied in any engine (TRAJECTORY_HOW_WE_GOT_TO_AC_2026-07-25.md:173). Gap 1 is the missing edge that guarantees the same outcome in the new architecture, and it is a regression: the only crawl this project ever validated gripped cortex nodes straight to collagen (ff_crawl_on_substrate.py:159,187).

THE SECOND STRUCTURAL PATTERN - PULL EVERYWHERE, PUSH NOWHERE. Gaps 2, 3 and 5 are one family. The 32-connector graph declares ATTACHMENT connectors almost everywhere (tethers, clutches, motors, LINC, plectin) and only THREE CONTACT connectors, all on the membrane's OUTER face (lamellipodium tip, filopodium tip, ECM). There is not one intracellular non-penetration edge. Because co-location in an array is explicitly not a connection, the cell can pull on itself everywhere and push on itself almost nowhere: the nucleus cannot be squeezed by the flattening cortex, the bilayer can pass through the cortical shell, and interior MTs get no lateral elastic support. Three recorded failures - nuclear flatten 0.0% with tether spokes buckling in compression (IF_CAGE_2026-07-16.md:19-26), the ERM "proven inert" at the resting setpoint (RESTING_BASELINE_DIAGNOSIS_2026-07-23c.md:137-138), and "nucleus/MT = decoupled passenger" (report4_actin_cortex_mechanics.md:678,691) - are symptoms of this ONE hole, not three separate bugs. One new ConnectorFamily.STERIC_CONTACT with three edges (nucleus<->cortex, nucleus<->membrane, membrane<->cortex) closes all three; the membrane<->cortex one is already written into SURFACE_BODY_PLAN.md:197-199,394 and was simply never promoted into contracts.py.

CHEAPEST PATH TO THE PI'S TWO NAMED TARGETS. (i) "cortex genuinely connected so it deforms/crumples as one object" needs gap 3 (so cortex and bilayer act as one surface rather than a slack tether pair) plus gap 1 (so the crumpling shell has something to react against). (ii) "lamellipodium forms, the cell remodels the ECM and moves forward" already has every edge it needs - traces (b) and (h) both close - and adding gap 1 is what converts cortical contractility from a cancelled internal tension into the rear half of the locomotory dipole. Total contract change: six new connectors (cortex_fa_anchor, membrane_cortex_contact, nucleus_cortex_contact, nucleus_membrane_contact, if_cortex_plectin, if_mt_plectin), 32 -> 38, ONE new family, and only two new rate cards - both plectin, both reusing the card if_sf_plectin already names. Gaps 6 and 7 are deliberately deferrable.

WHAT I DID NOT AUDIT. Implementation status is out of scope by the standard of evidence (19 of 32 connectors declared-only, net 2 of 32 dispatched - AUDIT_AC_ENGINE_2026-07-25.md:20-62). None of the seven gaps above is a restatement of an evidence-ladder rung: each is a connector that does not exist in the declared graph at all, and each names a structure, its two endpoints, and a measurable that would be wrong.

gaps.structure: Nuclear-envelope steric (non-penetration) contact against the actomyosin cortex and the inner membrane — i.e. any CONTACT-family connector with `nucleus` as an endpoint.
gaps.connects: nucleus (envelope surface) <-> cortex (basal + dorsal F-actin shell); and nucleus <-> membrane
gaps.why_architecture_cannot_express_it: `nucleus` has exactly FOUR edges in the graph and none of them is a contact: nucleus_cytosol_boundary (FLUID_BOUNDARY, ac/engine/contracts.py:269) and three LINC bonds to sf_arc / microtubule / intermediate_filament (contracts.py:291, :298, :311). There is NO cortex<->nucleus and NO membrane<->nucleus edge of ANY family. ConnectorFamily.CONTACT is declared (contracts.py:40) but instantiated only three times — lamellipodium_membrane_contact (:345), filopodium_membrane_tip (:372), membrane_ecm_contact (:446) — none touching nucleus or cortex. A LINC connector is a discrete nesprin/SUN bond at scattered sites (endpoint_role_b = 'nuclear-envelope LINC actin-facing site'), not an envelope-wide unilateral constraint, and it attaches to sf_arc, not to the cortex. The cytosol FLUID_BOUNDARY is a Biot/Darcy pressure+flux condition: on a finite-volume grid it cannot resolve the vanishing lubrication film, cannot enforce non-penetration, and carries no contact shear. The incumbent path confirms the hole rather than filling it: ac/cell/assemble.py:19-21 declares the all-filament WCA channel and then states 'Myosin/nucleus/membrane particles are marked dormant (active<0) so EV acts on actin nodes only', and assemble.py:24 calls the LINC tether 'nucleus<->cortex, the single load path'. ac/nucleus/INTEGRATION.md:76-78 proposes to route envelope<->cortex-filament steric through the SHARED global StericForce array — which is precisely the 'co-location in one shared array = implicit weld' pattern CLAUDE.md forbids, and which would have no connector declaration, no adjoint/work check, no ledger contribution, and no accepted-step transaction participation. Adding it therefore requires a 33rd connector, not a flag flip.
gaps.observable_that_would_be_wrong: A spread adherent MCF7 has spread height 3-5 um and a nucleus of comparable or larger diameter, so the nucleus is in hard contact with both the dorsal and the basal cortex. Without the edge: nuclear height / projected nuclear area / nuclear flattening under spreading come out wrong or unbounded, the envelope can interpenetrate the cortex and the plasma membrane, and the cell-height floor set by the nucleus does not exist. During crawl the nucleus cannot be squeezed, steered, or ratcheted by the cortex, so confinement response is absent. Literature the observable is measured against: Khatau et al. 2009 PNAS 106:19017 (perinuclear actin cap regulates nuclear shape); Versaevel, Grevesse & Gabriele 2012 Nat Commun 3:671 (cell-shape -> nuclear-shape coupling); Lomakin et al. 2020 Science 370:eaba2894 (nucleus/cell-surface CONTACT is the ruler that senses spatial constraint). This is the PI's stated priority failing at the largest compartment pair in the cell.

gaps.why_architecture_cannot_express_it: The cell's ONLY two edges to anything outside itself are integrin_collagen_clutch (contracts.py:279, reached via focal_adhesion) and membrane_ecm_contact (contracts.py:446). Both require the `ecm` component. There is no extracellular fluid component: `cytosol` is strictly the interior field — ac/fluid/domain.py:44-45 defines MembraneMaskProvider as classifying each grid cell 'inside (FLUID) or outside (OUTSIDE) the live outer membrane', and the domain is membrane-minus-nucleus. `world_boundary` is declared owns_geometry=False, dynamically_evolving=False (contracts.py:247-250) so it cannot BE a surface, and it has exactly one edge in the entire graph — ecm_far_field_anchor (contracts.py:440-444); a grep of all of ac/ for 'world_boundary' returns only that anchor and its validators. So there is no component and no edge that could carry either medium drag or a rigid external constraint, and adding one is a new component + new connector, not a declaration change.
gaps.observable_that_would_be_wrong: (a) Whole-cell rigid-body translation and rotation are undamped, unconstrained null modes of the inertialess coupled operator whenever the bound-clutch set is sparse or momentarily empty — at initialization, during full rear release, and for any detached/suspended state. This is not hypothetical: it is the exact recorded failure class of the only native crawl the project ever ran. FF_CRAWL_DIAGNOSIS_2026-07-09.md:39-55 records that the physically-correct whole-cell drag Sigma-gamma = 6*pi*eta*R could not be imposed in-solver ('rigid-body modes go unregularized -> NaN') and that the post-hoc COM-drag override produced 767 um in 30 s of runaway; and the crawl force balance the project actually used, F_net = gamma_COM * v with gamma_COM = 6*pi*eta*R (MDA_MB_231_MIGRATION_ROOTCAUSE_2026-07-14.md:10-17), has no home anywhere in the 13/32 graph. Note the poroelastic drag through the four *_cytosol_transfer edges cannot substitute: cytosol is INTERNAL to the cell, so that coupling is self-balancing for the cell's translation mode and supplies zero external damping. (b) No non-ECM external load can be applied at all: fluid shear on an epithelium, AFM / parallel-plate compression, micropipette aspiration, microchannel or PDMS-ceiling confinement, optical/magnetic tweezers. The project's own AFM and plate-compression validation geometry is therefore inexpressible in the engine graph, and the 'nucleus as ruler' confinement assay (Lomakin 2020) is doubly blocked (this gap + gap 1).

gaps.proposed_fix: Two separable additions. (i) A 14th ENVIRONMENT component `extracellular_medium` (Stokes/Brinkman exterior, or at minimum a boundary-integral surface mobility) with a `membrane_medium_traction` connector — magnitude is negligible (~1e-5 pN at 30 nm/s) but it is the physically correct regularizer of the six whole-cell rigid modes and the only way to load the cell with flow. (ii) Give `world_boundary` optional geometry (owns_geometry=True) plus a `membrane_world_contact` CONTACT connector for rigid-instrument assays, keeping it explicitly labelled a control geometry per LOAD_PATH_PLAN.md:106. Honest caveat: while the cell is well adhered with thousands of bound clutches the null modes are constrained, so this is blocking at the transitions and for assays rather than continuously.

gaps.structure: Integrin-adhesion anchorage of the basal cortical actin network — a `cortex` actin-side port on a focal adhesion.
gaps.connects: cortex (ventral/basal F-actin shell) <-> focal_adhesion (actin-side state)
gaps.why_architecture_cannot_express_it: focal_adhesion's actin-side ports are ONLY sf_arc (fa_actin_anchor, contracts.py:274), lamellipodium (lamellipodium_nascent_fa, :365) and filopodium (filopodium_nascent_fa, :392). There is no cortex<->focal_adhesion edge, and cortex has no ecm edge either (cortex's seven edges are membrane ERM :254, cytosol :259, sf_arc :285, microtubule capture :305, lamellipodium seam :352, filopodium root :379, nmii :406). So cortical tension can reach the substrate only in series through sf_cortex_transient — a finite-lifetime transient crosslink — plus a stress fiber plus fa_actin_anchor. Yet the `cortex` component owns the WHOLE 4*pi*R^2 shell including the ventral face by construction (CLAUDE.md's 70,686 = 100 um^-2 x 4*pi*(7.5 um)^2), so basal cortical filaments provably sit at the adhesion plane with no port to reach it. docs/v2_audit/cell_engine/LOAD_PATH_PLAN.md:96-106 shows the restriction is a deliberate anti-double-count design decision (it also forbids 'transverse arc -> FA' and welding SF to cortex), so this is a considered omission — but it is still a missing load path, and the two-hop substitute inserts a fictitious compliance.
gaps.observable_that_would_be_wrong: A spread cell with few or no stress fibers and no active protrusion — which is the MCF7 phenotype the baseline targets — generates ZERO adhesion traction, because every adhesion in the graph must be owned by sf_arc, lamellipodium or filopodium. Consequently the traction-force map, the cortical-tension contribution to substrate traction, and the spread-area force balance are structurally missing a channel; and nascent adhesions that assemble on the local ventral actin network outside a protrusion (Choi et al. 2008 Nat Cell Biol 10:1039, nascent adhesions assemble on the local actin/alpha-actinin network) cannot be represented at all.

Alternatively, PI ratifies a rule that all adhesion-competent ventral actin is by definition owned by sf_arc/lamellipodium and the cortex is dorsal/lateral only — in which case write that rule into contracts.py so the restriction is auditable rather than implicit.

gaps.structure: Plectin-sidearm crosslinks between the intermediate-filament network and microtubules (and, more broadly, the IF cage's peripheral anchorage to the cortex/membrane).
gaps.connects: intermediate_filament <-> microtubule (secondarily intermediate_filament <-> cortex / membrane)
gaps.why_architecture_cannot_express_it: `intermediate_filament` has exactly THREE edges: if_nucleus_linc (contracts.py:311), if_sf_plectin (:318), if_cytosol_transfer (:340). There is no IF<->MT edge, even though the mirror-image MT<->SF edge IS declared as mt_sf_spectraplakin (:324) and the same plectin chemistry family is already used on the IF<->SF edge ('plectin_if_actin', :321). There is also no IF<->cortex, IF<->membrane, or IF<->focal_adhesion edge. IF load can therefore reach the MT array only via IF -> sf_arc -> MT, so in a cell with few stress fibers the IF cage and the MT array are mechanically disconnected, and the IF network's only peripheral tie is through the SF population. Closing this needs a new connector.
gaps.observable_that_would_be_wrong: The tensegrity balance the PI ratified (2026-07-16: MT = compression struts, actin/IF = tension cables) cannot close directly between the two structural rigs, so MT buckling load and IF strain-stiffening are carried by the wrong series path or not at all. Specifically, vimentin templating of the MT array — the mechanism that sets directional persistence in migration (Gan et al. 2016 Cell Systems 3:252, 'Vimentin intermediate filaments template microtubule networks to enhance persistence in cell polarity and directed migration') — has no representation, so crawl directional persistence and the IF contribution to whole-cell stiffness under large deformation come out wrong. Primary structural citation for the missing crosslink itself: Svitkina, Verkhovsky & Borisy 1996 J Cell Biol 135:991, 'Plectin sidearms mediate interaction of intermediate filaments with microtubules and other components of the cytoskeleton'.
gaps.evidence: ac/engine/contracts.py:226-227, :311, :318-322, :324-328, :340-343; docs/v2_audit/cell_engine/CELL_ENGINE_ARCHITECTURE.md:32-40 (mermaid: IF edges go only to NUC and SF); docs/v2_audit/cell_engine/INTERMEDIATE_FILAMENT_PLAN.md.

If the IF cage is also to be peripherally anchored, add `if_cortex_plectin` on the same pattern; note the hemidesmosomal (alpha6beta4/plectin/keratin) IF->ECM route is deliberately NOT proposed because it requires laminin-332 and is outside the ratified collagen-I / alpha2beta1 baseline.

gaps.structure: The lamellipodium-to-transverse-arc (lamella) mechanical seam — the contractile actin arcs that form at the lamellipodium base out of lamellipodial network material and pull the leading edge back.
gaps.connects: lamellipodium (rear network) <-> sf_arc (transverse arc / dorsal SF)
gaps.why_architecture_cannot_express_it: `lamellipodium` has five edges: membrane contact (contracts.py:345), cortex rear seam (:352), cytosol transfer (:359), nascent FA (:365), NMII motor (:413). There is no lamellipodium<->sf_arc edge; the graph declares the lamellipodium's rear boundary as seaming to `cortex` instead (endpoint_role_a 'lamellipodial network rear seam' -> 'cortical actin material point'). Both substitute routes insert a third component in series: lam -> cortex -> sf_cortex_transient -> sf_arc, or lam -> focal_adhesion -> fa_actin_anchor -> sf_arc. Note also that LOAD_PATH_PLAN.md:100 forbids 'transverse arc -> FA', which closes the second route for arcs specifically (it remains open only for dorsal SFs), leaving arcs reachable from the lamellipodium ONLY through the cortex.
gaps.observable_that_would_be_wrong: The periodic protrusion-retraction cycle of the leading edge — arc contraction acting on the lamellipodial network — cannot be produced, so leading-edge advance rate and the amplitude/periodicity of edge retraction are wrong, and arc genesis from lamellipodial material has no mechanical seam to form across. Literature: Hotulainen & Lappalainen 2006 J Cell Biol 173:383 (transverse arcs are generated from the Arp2/3 lamellipodial network); Burnette et al. 2011 Nat Cell Biol 13:371 ('A role for actin arcs in the leading-edge advance of migrating cells'); Giannone et al. 2004 Cell 116:431 (periodic lamellipodial contractions).

gaps.proposed_fix: Declare `lamellipodium_arc_seam` (ConnectorFamily.TRANSIENT_ACTIN, lamellipodium <-> sf_arc, kinetics=True, commit_on_accept=True, chemistry_card='transient_actin_crosslink', endpoint roles 'lamellipodial network rear seam' <-> 'transverse arc material point'), i.e. the same shape as lamellipodium_cortex_seam but targeting the arc population. Keep the cortex seam as well — both exist in a real cell.

confirmed_sufficient: (1) THE LOCOMOTORY FORCE DIPOLE IS EXPRESSIBLE, and both halves of the never-applied ff/ fix are structurally present. Front half: lamellipodium_membrane_contact (contracts.py:345, chemistry_card='actin_membrane_brownian_ratchet_contact') generates the protrusive push; its retrograde reaction is held by lamellipodium_nascent_fa (:365) -> focal_adhesion -> integrin_collagen_clutch (:279) -> ecm -> ecm_far_field_anchor (:440) -> world_boundary. Rear half: nmii_cortex_motor (:406) + nmii_sf_motor (:399) contract while sf_arc is held forward by fa_actin_anchor (:274) and rear clutches release on the same catch-slip edge. This is exactly the two-part fix specified in MDA_MB_231_MIGRATION_ROOTCAUSE_2026-07-14.md:82-94 ('rear-retraction traction' + 'uncancelled front anchorage').

(1b) The ff/ cancellation mechanism is structurally cured. The recorded root cause was that the polarized channel's reaction 'lands on the MOVABLE collagen node, which the spring then drags the cell back toward' (MDA_MB_231_MIGRATION_ROOTCAUSE_2026-07-14.md:51-55). In the 13/32 graph the gripped collagen node is elastically continuous through ecm_crosslink (contracts.py:434) to a far-field Dirichlet pin whose constraint reaction R = -f is explicitly recorded per pinned node BEFORE the force is zeroed (ac/engine/ecm_world.py:396-450, FarFieldDirichletBoundaryRuntime), and GlobalCellLedger keeps reaction_resultant and traction_resultant INDEPENDENTLY sourced so 'sum to zero' is checked, not assumed (ac/engine/ledger.py:14-30). ECMWorldSettings hard-rejects an unanchored finite ECM (ecm_world.py:147-148).

(2) FRONT/REAR ASYMMETRY HAS A REPRESENTATION — geometric, in the instance rather than the schema, which is sufficient. lamellipodium and filopodium are declared 'local adaptive' components (contracts.py:228-237), so instantiating one at one pole makes the nascent-FA edges (:365, :392) exist only at the front; focal_adhesion owns per-plaque maturation state (CELL_ENGINE_ARCHITECTURE.md:65 'catch/slip state, maturation, integrin occupancy'), giving front-vs-rear adhesion lifetime asymmetry; rear release is force-gated on the clutch. That is precisely the emergent self-reinforcing polarity the project already ratified (FF_POLARIZED_CRAWL_DESIGN_2026-07-09.md sections 1-2). What does NOT exist is any owner of a persistent cell-scale polarity AXIS: 'polarized' appears only as a CellState label (ac/engine/cell_state.py:219) and CellState is structurally forbidden from emitting anything spatial or mechanical - it emits scalar Rate/Distribution keyed only by (component, reaction) and rejects force/pos/tension/count/topology targets (cell_state.py:43-55, :183-205). A graded Rac/Rho polarity signal would have to be a cytosol transported species (CELL_ENGINE_ARCHITECTURE.md:63, roadmap R7). Not reported as a gap: it is chemistry, not a mechanical load path.

(3) NO 14th SUBSTRATE COMPONENT IS NEEDED for the PI's target. A 2D compliant ECM instance is already expressible: ff/ecm_library.py:1 is explicitly 'multi-material, 2D/3D, alignment-controlled', dim=2 is a 'thin planar sheet' with nematic alignment control (ecm_library.py:502-541), a spatial-stiffness-gradient durotaxis lattice exists (:666-674), and ac/engine/ecm_world.py:41 already imports ECMSpec from it. ecm_far_field_anchor (contracts.py:440) supplies the momentum sink; membrane_ecm_contact (:446) supplies the basal steric floor via a real segment-surface contact protocol with adjoint scatter (ecm_world.py:320-345). The project has already ruled the rigid fixed-anchor substrate out of production (LOAD_PATH_PLAN.md:106 'FA | fixed world point | diagnostic rigid-substrate control only | non-production'; ECM_WORLD_PLAN.md:300). The only residual is rigid INSTRUMENT geometry, which is folded into gap 2.

(4) ECM REMODELLING IS A CLOSED LOOP - traced end to end. Plastic channel: ecm_crosslink (contracts.py:434-438) is INTERNAL/FIBER_CROSSLINK with kinetics=True, commit_on_accept=True, generation_required=True, remap_on_accept=True, blocks_sleep_refine=True, so force-gated crosslink unbind/rebind gives permanent realignment, densification and residual set. Damage channel: ecm owns segment_damage_d (ecm_world.py:595, :640) and ECMWorldSettings raises unless remodelling_enabled and damage_enabled (ecm_world.py:139-152, 'production ECM requires remodelling and damage state'). Permanence: commit_irreversible is documented as 'the only place a remesh can change the committed segment rest lengths / active set and bump topology_epoch_d', and it then calls refresh_mechanics_parameters(), which re-derives k_seg = EA/seg_rest and alpha = kappa/seg^3 from the NEW committed topology (ecm_world.py:714-742) - so the permanent change literally becomes the new constitutive operator. Feedback to the cell: both cell->ECM edges are live material-point endpoints with remap_on_accept - integrin_collagen_clutch (contracts.py:279-283, endpoint 'collagen ligand material point', barycentric per ecm_world.py:8-11) and membrane_ecm_contact (:446-450). So the cell pulls fibers, the fibers permanently rearrange, and the cell then feels the rearranged matrix as its boundary condition.

(4b) REAR RELEASE is integrin_collagen_clutch (contracts.py:279) bond rupture, and rupture is currently the ONLY disassembly channel - which is a real risk but NOT an architecture gap. Every component is declared has_events=False and contracts.py:192-196 states this is a deliberate per-component biology-phase decision awaiting a sourced rate, so focal_adhesion can own plaque-level assembly/disassembly the moment that flag is flipped. Flagged loudly because rupture-only rear release is exactly the documented ff/ failure ('the rear edge merely unbinds (zero force) instead of retracting the body forward', MDA_MB_231_MIGRATION_ROOTCAUSE_2026-07-14.md:57-59, :68-72) and because the front-biased-rebind workaround over-de-adhered and made the crawl WORSE (FF_CRAWL_DIAGNOSIS_2026-07-09.md:30-33). Without plaque-level irreversible disassembly, a fully ruptured rear adhesion can immediately re-nucleate through the nascent-FA edges and the rear never truly releases.

(5) THE PROPULSION OBSERVABLE EXISTS AT ARCHITECTURE LEVEL; only the diagnostic is missing. GlobalCellLedger.traction_resultant is 'Sum of the cell->ECM clutch/contact load actually scattered onto the ECM body' and reaction_resultant is the far-field Dirichlet reaction, with a device-side balance gate against a caller-supplied tolerance (ac/engine/ledger.py:14-30, :240-282, :329-336). world_boundary (contracts.py:247-250, 'physiological far-field reference frame') supplies the inertial frame that makes centroid displacement well-defined. What is absent is instrumentation, not structure: grep over ac/ finds no cell-centroid / COM-displacement / spread-area observable anywhere (only per-fiber centroids at ac/weave/stress_fiber.py:289 and ac/emergence/synthetic.py), and ROLLING_ROADMAP.md R1-R15 contains no migration or translocation scenario - R9's perturbation matrix (ROLLING_ROADMAP.md:304-311) lists 'protrusion growth/retraction' and 'adhesion formation/maturation/release' but never whole-cell displacement. Writing a centroid/traction-dipole observable is a diagnostic task, correctly not on the 8-state ladder.

THE ff/ GRID-DRAG PATHOLOGY IS STRUCTURALLY DISSOLVED (a genuine architectural win). ff/'s v proportional to 1/Nc came from assigning the NF2007 single-fiber log-drag per node so the whole-cell COM drag scaled with node count (FF_CRAWL_DIAGNOSIS_2026-07-09.md:39-41). In the 13/32 graph dissipation enters only through physical poroelastic couplings - surface_porous_transfer (contracts.py:259) and the four *_cytosol_transfer IMMERSED_TRANSFER edges (:330, :335, :340, :359, :386) - i.e. real filament-through-pore-fluid drag, which is grid-convergent, not grid-proportional. There is no per-node gamma in the graph at all. The flip side is gap 2: because cytosol is internal, this drag is self-balancing for the whole-cell translation mode.

ACTIN MASS RECYCLING FOR A SUSTAINED CRAWL NEEDS NO OWNERSHIP TRANSFER, so the disjoint-population invariant (PI 2026-07-22) does not obstruct crawl. The lamellipodium owns severing and capping event channels (ac/engine/protrusion.py:52-57), monomer returns to the cytosol G-actin field through lamellipodium_cytosol_transfer (contracts.py:359-363, endpoint 'active filament quadrature and barbed-end sink' <-> 'porous drag and G-actin transport stencil'), and the cortex re-nucleates from the same field. Front growth and rear disassembly therefore conserve mass through the shared field without any filament ever changing component, so each physical filament stays in exactly one component.

MMP / PERICELLULAR PROTEOLYSIS IS NOT REPORTED AS A GAP. The membrane<->ecm edge already exists with generation_required=True and remap_on_accept=True (contracts.py:446-450), and ConnectorContract supports kinetics + chemistry_card + commit_on_accept (contracts.py:83-119), so cell-localized MT1-MMP fiber scission is a declaration change on an existing edge, not a missing structure. Flagged as the single thing standing between this graph and 3D confined invasion, where collagen pore size is below the nuclear diameter and proteolysis is the difference between moving and not moving - relevant to the MDA-MB-231 scope, not to the MCF7 2D-crawl question as posed.

CELL-CELL JUNCTIONS ARE ABSENT (no junction component, no cell-to-cell edge anywhere in the 13/32 graph). Correctly out of scope for the single-cell question, but recorded because the PI named EMT progression as a target: without a cadherin adherens-belt connector and a desmosome IF<->IF edge, EMT can only be represented as a change in the single cell's own cytoskeletal composition (keratin -> vimentin, expressible), never as the loss of a load-bearing junction.

MT-TARGETED FOCAL-ADHESION DISASSEMBLY has no microtubule<->focal_adhesion edge, and is deliberately EXCLUDED from the gap list because the mechanism is dynamin/clathrin-mediated trafficking rather than a mechanical load path (Kaverina, Krylyshkina & Small 1999 J Cell Biol 146:1033; Ezratty, Partridge & Gundersen 2005 Nat Cell Biol 7:581). Recorded only because it is the physiological timer for rear release, i.e. it is the signalling counterpart of the concern raised in (4b).

THE CORTEX ITSELF IS ADEQUATELY CONNECTED for the PI's worked example (i) 'the cortex deforms/crumples as one object': seven edges (membrane ERM :254, cytosol porous transfer :259, sf_arc transient :285, MT dynein capture :305, lamellipodium seam :352, filopodium root :379, NMII motor :406), with intra-cortex crosslinks and turnover as declared component-internal state (CELL_ENGINE_ARCHITECTURE.md:61). Whether it actually crumples as one object is a percolation/implementation question already tracked, not an architecture question.

THE ARCHITECTURE PROVIDES ITS OWN PATH-EXISTENCE CHECK. CellArchitecture.force_path (contracts.py:162-176) does BFS over the declared connector graph, and mechanical_group (:178-183) deduplicates composite series joints (the alpha2beta1_collagen_series is one runtime object bound under both fa_actin_anchor and integrin_collagen_clutch, ac/engine/composition.py:20-24) so a series clutch is never double-counted. Every connector is validated bidirectional and adjoint-required at construction (contracts.py:110-111, :90-91), and a kinetic connector that does not commit only on an accepted step is a hard build error (:106-109). The graph machinery is sound; the findings above are missing EDGES in it, not defects in it.
result.notes:
SCOPE AND METHOD. I read the 13/32 declaration in full (ac/engine/contracts.py:186-452), enumerated each component's neighbour set by hand from that source, then traced each candidate load path against the concrete runtimes (ecm_world.py, protrusion.py, ledger.py, cell_state.py, composition.py, load_path.py, forces_manifest.py, fluid/domain.py) and against the ff/ crawl post-mortems taken as measured fact. I applied the stated standard strictly: I dropped four candidates that survive as expressible-but-unimplemented (MMP scission via flipping kinetics on the existing membrane_ecm_contact edge; FA plaque disassembly via focal_adhesion has_events; polarity as a cytosol transported species; frictional tangential contact within the existing CONTACT family) and two that fail the 'real cell HAS it' test for this baseline (hemidesmosomal IF->ECM anchorage, which needs laminin-332 and not collagen-I/alpha2beta1; rigid dish geometry, which the cell does not have - folded into gap 2 as an assay limitation).

BOTTOM LINE ON LENS 4. The 13/32 graph CAN express a cell that forms a lamellipodium, remodels the ECM, and moves forward. The two things ff/ lacked are both present as declared edges: the reaction sink is ecm_far_field_anchor into world_boundary with an explicit per-node Dirichlet reaction ledger, and the rear-retraction half is nmii_cortex_motor + nmii_sf_motor pulling against front-held fa_actin_anchor with rear clutch release. The ff/ crawl failure was a force-model failure inside one engine, not a missing architectural structure. The graph is also structurally immune to the grid-drag pathology, because dissipation is poroelastic rather than per-node.

WHAT ACTUALLY BLOCKS CRAWL IS THE ONE THING NOBODY ADDED: the cell has no external environment except the ECM. Every edge leaving the cell terminates on `ecm`. That leaves the six whole-cell rigid modes undamped and unconstrained whenever adhesion is sparse - which is exactly the NaN / 767-um-runaway pair recorded in FF_CRAWL_DIAGNOSIS_2026-07-09.md:43-55 - and it makes the project's own 6*pi*eta*R force balance homeless. It also makes every rigid-instrument validation assay (AFM, plates, micropipette, confinement) inexpressible, which is a separate problem worth surfacing on its own.

RANKING FOR THE PI, given the stated priority (connectedness over magnitude). Gap 1 (nucleus has no contact edge to cortex or membrane) is the one that directly contradicts 'compartments must deform each other': the largest deformable compartment in the cell is held to the cytoskeleton by discrete LINC tethers alone, the incumbent explicitly marks the nucleus dormant in the only steric channel (assemble.py:19-21), and the proposed alternative (a shared global WCA array, ac/nucleus/INTEGRATION.md:78) is the co-location-equals-weld pattern the engine exists to forbid. Gap 2 is the crawl blocker. Gaps 3-5 are all of one shape - a real load path that exists but is routed through a third component - and each is a one-line ConnectorContract addition; none needs a new component.

TWO OBSERVATIONS THAT ARE NOT GAPS BUT ARE WORTH THE PI'S ATTENTION. (a) Declaration asymmetry: sf_arc's internal crosslinks are declared as a first-class connector (dorsal_arc_crosslink, contracts.py:429) and the ECM's are too (ecm_crosslink, :434), but the cortex's crosslinks are undeclared component-internal state. Both choices are defensible, but the inconsistency means a reader cannot tell from contracts.py which intra-component couplings are audited by the connector machinery. (b) The roadmap has no migration stage. R6 binds protrusion actors, R9 exercises 'protrusion growth/retraction', but nothing in R1-R15 asks the cell to translocate, and no centroid observable exists in ac/. The PI's worked example (ii) - lamellipodium forms, ECM remodels, cell moves forward - currently has no gate anywhere on the ladder. That is the cheapest high-value addition after the two blocking gaps: a crawl scenario in R9 plus a centroid/traction-dipole observable fed from the existing traction_resultant and reaction_resultant ledger slots.

result.summary:
VERDICT: PARTIALLY_REFUTED — the adversary's verdict (SUFFICIENT_WITH_CAVEATS) holds, but its one gap must be cut down from two connectors and a broad "surface bears on nucleus" claim to ONE connector and ONE constraint.

Reverse-error check first: this lens did NOT count component names. It quoted 15+ file:line locations that I independently verified (contracts.py:36 CONTACT family; CELL_ENGINE_ARCHITECTURE.md:90-91 and :211; ac/solid/INTEGRATION.md:92-93 "the I7 LINC tether is a *distinct* force family ... NOT a steric term"; FLUID_CORE_PLAN.md:21-22 nucleus 642-node mesh retained for "collision"; INTERMEDIATE_FILAMENT_PLAN.md:53-55; SURFACE_BODY_PLAN.md:219-220; ECM_WORLD_PLAN.md:81-88 far_field_dirichlet and :300 fixed-anchor 폐기; assemble.py:19-21 and 812-820 EV dormant mask; INTERNAL_DISPLACEMENT_DIAGNOSIS_2026-07-16.md:13-22). Every one is accurate as quoted. It also traced named connector chains front-to-rear rather than asserting reachability.

MY OWN INDEPENDENT SWEEP. I ran reference_cell_architecture() and enumerated all C(13,2)=78 pairs: 30 declared, 48 absent. I then asked of each of the 48 "is this a real DIRECT structure, and is there a series route through declared pairs?" Result: 47 of 48 either are not a real direct structure (cortex-ecm, sf_arc-ecm, lamellipodium-ecm, filopodium-ecm, nucleus-ecm — membrane physically interposed; nmii-ecm, nucleus-nmii, focal_adhesion-nmii — no such structure; anything-world_boundary — an adherent cell's every external reaction passes through matrix) or have a series route through an existing pair (membrane-focal_adhesion via 1+7+5; cortex-focal_adhesion via 7+5 and 18+20; membrane-microtubule via 10+1; if-focal_adhesion via 12+5; if-cortex via 12+7; mt-if via 11+9 or 12+13; sf_arc-lamellipodium via 18+7; lamellipodium-filopodium via cortex/membrane). Exactly ONE absent pair has no deviatoric route at all: (cortex, nucleus). So the adversary's conclusion is reproducible — I could not find a 14th component either, and I could not find a second inexpressible load path.

WHERE I BREAK IT. (a) (membrane, nucleus) is refuted by the project's OWN geometry: assemble.py:28 / :126 "the membrane CONTAINS the cortex", R_CORTEX_UM = R_CELL_UM − gap (assemble.py:134). The cortex is always interposed, so the membrane can never bear on the envelope without the cortex bearing first — the identical interposition logic the adversary itself used to route lamellipodium→ECM through the membrane. It applied its own rule inconsistently. 32→33, not 32→34. (b) The actin-cap and MT portions of the load are in-architecture extensions, not gaps: pair 8 (sf_arc-nucleus) and pair 9 (microtubule-nucleus) EXIST, and MICROTUBULE_PLAN.md:184 already provisions "MT radius for collision with nucleus, cortex and other rods" — so the "collision geometry with no consumer connector" argument is 3/4 wrong; only the cortex consumer is missing. (c) The survivor must therefore be restated more narrowly than the adversary stated it: what is inexpressible is not "all cortex→nucleus load" (a 2-hop tether series cortex→7→sf_arc→8→nucleus does exist) but the UNILATERAL NON-PENETRATION CONSTRAINT of the cortex sheet itself on the envelope. A sparse series of tethers through a spatially localized SF/arc population cannot stop cortex nodes at a location with no cap fiber from passing through the nuclear surface.

SUFFICIENCIES I TRIED AND FAILED TO BREAK. result.summary: ADVERSARIAL VERDICT: the deformation-coupling lens found 6 gaps; 4 are REFUTED, 1 is correctly self-deprioritised, and only 1 survives — plus 1 the lens itself demoted below its bar that I judge under-rated. Its two headline gaps (no connector tangent; no coupled-candidate convergence obligation) are real observations but are NOT architecture gaps under the stated standard: neither is a load path, and both ARE expressible in the graph. Three of its five structural gaps are artifacts of ONE methodological error: it used `CellArchitecture.force_path` (contracts.py:162-175), a single-shortest-path BFS whose neighbour loop is `sorted(self.neighbors(current))` (contracts.py:172), so at equal hop count the alphabetically-first component wins — and "cytosol" sorts before "microtubule", "nucleus" and "sf_arc". Every time the lens reported "the only route goes through the CYTOSOL — a pore-pressure field that carries no deviatoric load", an equal-length SOLID route existed and was hidden by that tie-break. Re-running the same BFS with the two fluid families (IMMERSED_TRANSFER, FLUID_BOUNDARY) removed gives: intermediate_filament→cortex = (IF, sf_arc, cortex); IF→microtubule = (IF, nucleus, MT), also (IF, sf_arc, MT); nucleus→cortex = (nucleus, MT, cortex), also (nucleus, sf_arc, cortex); nucleus→ecm = (nucleus, sf_arc, focal_adhesion, ecm). actin/MT/IF are ALREADY one solid tri-network, and the nucleus is already solidly tied to the outer shell. I also enumerated every cortex→ecm simple path over non-fluid connectors: there are 6 fully adhesive routes of length ≤3, e.g. cortex→(sf_cortex_transient, contracts.py:285)→sf_arc→(fa_actin_anchor, :274)→focal_adhesion→(integrin_collagen_clutch, :279)→ecm, plus the lamellipodium and filopodium nascent-FA routes — so "the cortex has no adhesive path to the ECM at all" is false (the lens's own next sentence, "every adhesive route must pass through sf_arc/lamellipodium/filopodium", contradicts its headline). The lens did NOT commit the reverse error the brief warns about: it traced real code and computed real adjacencies, and its force-real/declared-only census (4/4/24) is stricter and better than the audit it was checking. Its failure was enumeration, not effort. ONE gap survives, and it is sharper than the lens's version: the nucleus can be PULLED and PRESSURISED but never PUSHED. All three nucleus↔solid edges are LINC-family tension tethers (actin_cap_linc :291, mt_nucleus_linc :298, if_nucleus_linc :311) and its only volumetric edge is nucleus_cytosol_boundary (:269, FLUID_BOUNDARY, kinetics=False, a draining Darcy/Biot field that cannot enforce a geometric constraint). All three CONTACT-family connectors in the 32 are lamellipodium_membrane_contact (:345), filopodium_membrane_tip (:372) and membrane_ecm_contact (:446) — none touches the nucleus. This is the ONE case where the missing interaction is not merely un-routed but SIGN-unavailable: the other missing edges the lens named (plectin IF↔cortex, fa↔membrane) have real solid indirect routes ≤2 extra hops, so deleting them changes magnitudes; there is no compressive nucleus↔shell path of ANY length. Corroborated at the incumbent level — the WCA steric mask sets every non-actin node dormant, "active<0 → EV skips myosin/nucleus/membrane" (ac/cell/assemble.py:818-819) — and by the fluid plan's own workaround, which compresses the nucleus with a "prescribed membrane compression/pulse" (cell_engine/FLUID_CORE_PLAN.md:311), exactly the one-way prescribed load the SoT rules out as a coupled path (CELL_ENGINE_ARCHITECTURE.md:135). I also promote one finding the lens explicitly put below its bar: there is no cell-facing external-load or rigid-boundary endpoint anywhere (world_boundary is owns_geometry=False, dynamically_evolving=False, contracts.py:249, adjacency {ecm} only), so a rigid coverslip, AFM cantilever, compression plate, micropipette or confining channel wall has no home — and that is precisely how the PI's example (i), "the cortex crumples as one object", would be demonstrated. Two sufficiencies I tried hardest to break and could not: cortex-as-one-object is genuinely component-internal (percolating crosslink network + Cytosim bending + all-fiber WCA self-contact, forces_manifest.py:260-262), and the crawl chain is genuinely topologically complete — the front/rear asymmetry that prevents the old isotropic-cancellation failure has a declared home in two DISTINCT chemistry cards (actin_talin_integrin at contracts.py:277 vs actin_talin_integrin_nascent at :350 and :377), so lateral cancellation is now a kinetics outcome, not a topology defect. One thing I checked and will not report as a gap because the project already tracks it: cortex's IMMERSED_TRANSFER endpoint role is "porous-fluid transfer stencil" only (contracts.py:189-190) while the protrusion ones say "G-actin transport stencil", so cortex disassembly cannot refill the monomer pool sustained protrusion drains — but that is the known, PI-pending 32→36 CHEMICAL_FLUX wiring (monomer_flux.py:303-311 lists cortex/sf_arc/lamellipodium/filopodium consumers), and it is a chemical flux, not a mechanical load path. Read-only throughout; no file edited, no git write command run.

Enumerating every simple cortex->ecm path over non-fluid connectors gives SIX fully adhesive routes of length <=3: cortex-(sf_cortex_transient :285)-sf_arc-(fa_actin_anchor :274)-FA-(integrin_collagen_clutch :279)-ecm; the same via lamellipodium_cortex_seam (:352) + lamellipodium_nascent_fa (:365); the same via filopodium_cortex_root (:379) + filopodium_nascent_fa (:386); every link kinetic and commit_on_accept.
